#1857. Crystal Palace learn Jean-Philippe Mateta appeal verdict after Tottenham red card

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Crystal Palace have failed with their appeal against Jean-Philippe Mateta’s red card against Tottenham.

The French striker will serve a three-match suspension following his early dismissal during Saturday’s 2-0 loss in north London.

Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute for a lunging challenge on Tottenham captain Micky van de Ven, making contact with his ankle.

He was shown a straight red card by referee Michael Oliver following a VAR review, having initially only been booked, leaving struggling Palace to play most of the match against resurgent Spurs with 10 men.

Palace believed that the contact was accidental and launched an appeal in a bid to get Mateta’s ban overturned ahead of Sunday’s pivotal visit of Liverpool to Selhurst Park in the Premier League.

However, that has now been rejected by the Football Association (FA), meaning he will be absent against Liverpool and for the following two top-flight matches that take place after the November international break - against Coventry and Hull.

“An independent regulatory commission has dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment in relation to Jean-Philippe Mateta,” the FA said in a statement.

The suspension does not apply to European competition, so Mateta will be free to play in Palace’s upcoming Europa League games against Hoffenheim and Real Sociedad.

The 29-year-old has made five appearances across all competitions so far this term, scoring once and spending time out with a hamstring injury.

His latest absence in the Premier League is another huge blow for under-fire Eagles manager Pierre Sage, whose future at the club remains subject to severe scrutiny before facing Liverpool and heading into another international break.

#1856. James Milner runs New York Marathon in three hours and nine minutes - just months after retiring from football at 40 - after using AI training programme

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 07:49 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 07:49 EDT, 2 November 2026

James Milner may only be a few months retired as a professional footballer, but he showcased he is still an elite athlete after partaking in his first-ever marathon at the weekend.

Milner swapped his football boots for his running shoes on Sunday as he competed in the New York Marathon.

And the 40-year-old clocked an impressive time running the 26.2-mile route on his debut at three hours, nine minutes and four seconds.

The former Leeds, Newcastle, Aston Villa, Manchester City, Liverpool and Brighton midfielder was running for the James Milner Foundation - which has raised over £1.3million previously for various charities such as the NSPCC and Help for Heroes.

And speaking ahead of the race, Milner revealed that he had been using AI as his main training-base tool.

Asked about his long run in preparation for the New York Marathon, the former England international told Let's Run: 'Longest I've done is just over 32 kilometers. I hit 30 another couple of times, and then just used AI really for a training program.

James Milner ran the New York Marathon in three hours, nine minutes and four seconds

Milner only retired from football at the end of last season, finishing his career at Brighton

He won 11 major honours in his career, including the Champions League at Liverpool in 2018-19

'That's how it started, yeah. I know a few other people and stuff, but yeah, just bounced things off that really and went from there.'

It is unclear if all-time Premier League appearance holder Milner (658 games), who turns 41 in January, will run another marathon again in the future - but when that prospect was proposed to him, he revealed the training for it has helped him adjust to the realities of no longer playing professionally.

'I think it's one of them, after I've finished - hopefully - on Sunday, I'll either love it and have the bug and want to tick off loads of marathons, or maybe I'll hate it, never want to do another and maybe go to some triathlons or something else,' he continued.

'But fitness has always been a big part of my life, and I feel I've always been goal-orientated. I think I'd find it hard to not have a goal to train for, and I think this has been really important for me in terms of retiring and having something to aim for and training and still having that importance.

'Even when I was on holiday, [it was like] look, I need to get up and train for this. I need to eat the right things because I've got this run in the morning. I've lived that for 25 years. It's important for me to keep that going, and I feel very fortunate to be part of the New York Marathon. It's such a special city every time you're here.'

During a storied career, Milner won the Premier League twice with Manchester City before lifting the title as well as the Champions League with Liverpool.

In total Milner, who also had a loan spell at Swindon, won 11 major honours during his career alongside 61 England caps.

#1853. Who are Scott Parker's backroom team? West Ham legends reunite for new era

West Ham have announced the appointment of Scott Parker as their new head coach to replace Nuno Espirito Santo.

Parker quickly succeeds Nuno, who was sacked on Tuesday morning after West Ham’s 3-1 defeat by West Brom, as the Irons look to get their automatic promotion bid back on track.

The former West Ham midfielder is seen as a safe pair of hands given his knowledge of the club and vast previous experience in getting teams promoted from the Championship.

West Ham are currently eighth in the Championship table, having won six of their first 13 league games, and take on Cardiff on Wednesday night, with Parker set to be in the dugout.

The 46-year-old, who has been out of work since leaving Burnley in April following confirmation of their relegation from the Premier League, will be joined by first-team coaches Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Billy Lepine, while Mark Noble will also be working closely with the squad.

The permanent structure of Parker’s backroom staff has yet to be announced, but Standard Sport has assessed who will assist the former England international during his first game at the helm in Wales.

A club legend and former team-mate of Parker’s, Noble became West Ham’s sporting director in January 2023 but now looks set for a more hands-on role within the backroom team.

It is unclear just what job Noble, who made 550 appearances for West Ham as a player, will undertake and where he will fit in as Parker looks to settle on a permanent backroom structure over the coming weeks.

Another former West Ham player with more than 500 appearances to his name, Potts was promoted from academy coach to Nuno’s backroom team in October 2025 after impressing on an interim basis following the Portuguese’s arrival at the club.

He helped bridge the gap between the club’s academy and the first team, with Nuno handing chances to youngsters such as Freddie Potts, Mohamadou Kante, Airidas Golambeckis and Ezra Mayers last season.

Prenderville worked in West Ham’s academy before being promoted to Nuno’s backroom team last season.

He was part of the Under-18s coaching team in 2022/23 when West Ham won the FA Youth Cup, beating Arsenal 5-1 at the Emirates Stadium. Prenderville has played an important role in the development of several academy-turned-first-team players.

A West Ham fan, Lepine was appointed head of academy goalkeeping in November 2020 before being promoted to Nuno’s backroom team.

He worked alongside Nuno’s long-time assistant, Rui Barbosa, as a goalkeeping coach and helped Mads Hermansen re-establish himself as the club’s first-choice option after he was dropped from the side under Graham Potter.

#1852. Manchester United sent major JJ Gabriel update in transfer saga twist

Real Madrid believe they have won the race to sign Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel.

Gabriel, who turned 16 in October, decided in September to leave Man Utd after reportedly growing frustrated by a lack of first-team opportunities.

The teenager has given formal notice to cancel his registration with Man Utd after walking out on the club. He has since been training individually in Spain.

Gabriel will now be able to sign scholarship terms with another club, and Real Madrid are confident they have won the race for the highly rated youngster after stiff competition from Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich.

Gabriel's European Union passport is expected to make a move abroad easier.

United would be entitled to compensation if he leaves, although the amount would be lower should, as expected, he join a club outside the Premier League.

A transfer ‘fee’ of £8.5million has been reported elsewhere.

The forward has already built a strong reputation, scoring a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut and being named Premier League Under-18 Player of the Season last term, despite being only 14 for much of the campaign.

A United source previously described him as “the best 15-year-old in Europe”, while former interim manager Darren Fletcher said: “The world is his oyster.”

United head coach Michael Carrick has urged caution over the situation, stressing the importance of protecting the teenager's welfare and well-being.

But the transfer saga appears to be close to a conclusion.

Gabriel is expected to join Madrid's youth team, Castilla, who play in the second division of Spanish football, and would also play in the UEFA Youth League.

#1851. Mikel Arteta has Max Dowman conundrum to solve as Arsenal face Prague battle

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Prague will always hold a special place in Max Dowman's heart.

Aged 15 years and 308 days old, Dowman came on at the Fortuna Arena last season and in doing so became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League.

UEFA have been kind enough to mark the anniversary. Exactly a year on from that fixture, Arsenal are back at the same stadium to face Slavia Prague once again.

It has been an eventful 12 months for Dowman, who now has a Premier League medal in his possession, but it has been a particularly dramatic week.

The 16-year-old has served the first match of a three-game suspension for the straight red card he was shown against Fleetwood.

That ban does not apply to European competitions. Dowman played a full part in training on Tuesday and is part of the travelling squad in Prague.

The decision for Mikel Arteta is whether to hand Dowman a first Champions League start, or continue a period of tough love.

In response to criticism of his reaction to Dowman at Fleetwood, when he angrily spoke to the teenager as he walked off the pitch, Arteta made it clear that no allowances would be made for Dowman because of his age.

“This is the environment and this is the reality,” Arteta said.

“Otherwise we are in Disneyland, we are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League at this level and we look after him so much that you cannot imagine.

“But at the same time we are going to demand him, like to anybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play.”

Dowman cannot play in the Premier League until Arsenal host Manchester City on November 29, but the Champions League offers the chance for him to move on from that red card.

It was the second time in a month that Dowman had been sent off, having also been dismissed for England's Under-19s.

Arteta has been very clear that he has hammered home the message to Dowman that he must expect rough treatment and, more importantly, that he cannot react.

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal triple raid; Man Utd want Bellingham

Choose the right education path for your child

Those discussions will have continued since the Fleetwood red card and those thoughts will be front of Arteta's mind when he selects his lineup in Prague.

Before Tuesday night's fixtures in the Champions League, Slavia Prague ranked seventh out of the 36 teams in the competition for fouls committed. They are the only side to have been shown two red cards this season.

When the two teams met last season, the hosts committed 24 fouls. Dowman was barely on the pitch for 20 minutes and was fouled twice.

The approach Slavia Prague might adopt towards Dowman, then, is no great surprise. Particularly after his recent red cards, there will be a feeling that the teenager can be riled and will react to a physical test.

However, Arsenal are not flush with options. Bukayo Saka is out with a quad injury and Noni Madueke just about shook off an ankle issue in time to play the full 90 minutes at Anfield.

With Saka out, Madueke is a pivotal part of Arsenal's attack and they cannot afford for him to be injured. Dowman is now unable to ease the domestic load but he can allow Madueke a precious rest on Wednesday night.

Ordinarily, that would feel like a fairly obvious call for Arteta to make. The past week has perhaps complicated the situation and given Arteta more to ponder.

Does he leave Dowman on the bench, whether it be to send him a message or to protect him considering the current spotlight? Or does he show his faith in the teenager and trust him to learn the necessary lessons to keep a cooler head?

Arteta indicated at his pre-match press conference that he will opt for the latter and put the Fleetwood saga in the past.

“That’s a chapter that is gone,” Arteta said.

“It’s a moment of learning for all of us and we move on. You learn from the not so good ones, make sure you learn from the great ones as well. He’s been in great spirits.”

Against limited opposition and on a night where rotation is likely, it feels an ideal opportunity for Arteta to showcase his trust and Dowman to repay it.

#1850. “It’s not a surprise to me” – Pulisic delighted with Milan’s performance in derby win

Christian Pulisic believes AC Milan recorded an important win against Inter in the derby, but they must keep their heads down and continue working.

Milan claimed the bragging rights in the derby, winning 3-1 at San Siro tonight thanks to three goals in the first half. The first came from a Christian Pulisic header, the second was an Adrien Rabiot goal from a corner and the third was a Diego Moreira free-kick.

Alessandro Bastoni’s goal had briefly halved the deficit, but it was to be all for nothing as Milan racked up their fourth Derby della Madonnina win in a row. It moves the Rossoneri four points behind their city rivals, and also ends their unbeaten start to the season.

Pulisic spoke to DAZN after the full-time whistle to give his assessments on the game, and his words were relayed by MilanNews.

“We started the match very well, with intensity, with physicality. We played very well, scoring two goals in the first part, and this victory is very important for us.”

Four games, four goals, and four wins with Inter…

“I have to keep scoring in the derby, yes (laughs, ed.)”

“These are three very important points for us, but we have to continue to find this consistency and win every match.”

“Yes, we always play well in big games like today, so it’s not a surprise to me. We did things well.”

#1849. Jack Grealish latest: Everton boss David Moyes reveals whether Man City loanee features in his plan after disciplinary issue

By Ben Sully | 03 Nov 2026 00:12, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 03:56

Everton manager David Moyes has left the door open for Jack Grealish to reignite his career at the Hill Dickinson Stadium despite being punished for a disciplinary issue.

Grealish, who is currently in his second loan spell from Manchester City, was left out of the squad for Thursday's 3-1 EFL Cup win over Newcastle United due to a disciplinary breach.

Reports suggested Grealish was punished after failing to show for a training session in the lead-up to the midweek fixture.

Grealish's name was once again absent when Everton published their teamsheet for Monday's Premier League away clash against Newcastle.

Explaining the attacker's latest absence, Everton published a short statement on their official X account: "Jack Grealish is not match fit and therefore not part of tonight’s squad."

The Toffees went on to claim a 1-0 victory at St James' Park, moving them up to seventh spot in the Premier League table.

Questioned about Grealish's absence after the win, Moyes told BBC Sport: "He's unavailable at the moment, and we will make a decision with the club when we think that availability comes back."

When asked whether his omission was fitness-related, the Everton boss said: "All I'm giving out is that he is unavailable at the moment."

In his post-match press conference, Moyes admitted he was unsure whether Grealish would be back in the squad for Friday's home clash against Coventry City.

However, he was able to offer a clearer response when asked if there is a chance for the 31-year-old to return, telling reporters: “Of course there is, yes."

The upcoming meeting against Frank Lampard's side represents Everton's final game before the international break.

There is perhaps some sense in Everton keeping Grealish on the sidelines before bringing him back into the fold for the first game after the international window against Brentford.

That would give the club time to allow the situation to cool and offer Grealish time to try to earn some trust back in training over the two-week break.

#1848. Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand said everything you need to know about this moment...

Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town

Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City

United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

Martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

More substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

More changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by new signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

Milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

All square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs

United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

Shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

Carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

Estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

Milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely new cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

We are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

Manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

Marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE

Manchester United Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Tielemans, Santos, Fernandes; Amad, Dorgu; Cunha

Subs Heath, Mee, Amass, Dalot, Martínez, Yoro, Collyer, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Mainoo, Gabriel, Lacey, Mbeumo, Rashford, Zirkzee

AC Milan Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlović; Chukwueze, Jashari, Musah, Estupiñán; Loftus-Cheek, Cissè; Ramos

Subs Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Diawara, Vladimirov, Ricci, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Modrić, Comotto, Camarda

At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

“It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”

Welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri said Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

Was injured during the last international break but is back between the sticks now for Crystal Palace and therefore likely to dislodge Jason Steele as third-choice goalkeeper.

Scoring for fun for Leeds United and likely to get his chance for England again.

Not having a particularly good season at City from an individual perspective but is still clearly one of the country’s best centre-backs.

Versatile positionally, playing pretty regularly, and the scorer of the very first goal of Tuchel’s tenure back in March 2025.

A key man for Everton and a midfielder the England head coach is fond of. Could well get another chance for the national team this month.

Tuchel is a member of the Rio Ngumoha fan club, and the Liverpool winger would be unlucky to miss out this month.

Produced some solid performances at right-back last time out and will probably be in again.

Another player the head coach has always shown a liking to. Able to play through the middle or out on the left, and Marcus Rashford being out injured may prove no bad thing for his chances.

Not as integral to City under Enzo Maresca as he was under Pep Guardiola but a very popular England player sure to make it in.

Was absent from Chelsea’s 2-0 win over 10-man Manchester United due to illness but his form is likely to see him into the squad, despite 36 years of age, provided he has recovered from illness.

Going to be a beneficiary for club and country from Bukayo Saka’s injury. It will mean greater game time.

Tuchel remains frustrated with how many camps Palmer drops out of. Will he try once more to get the chance to work with him in the flesh this month?

Playing a fair amount at right-back for Arsenal and that is a position where England have problems after Reece James’s injury.

Tuchel was unable to call on him due to injury last time out but the Inter Milan man was a big part and a larger-than-life character in England’s run to the World Cup semi-finals.

It is pretty impossible to predict week to week what will happen next in the world of Kobbie Mainoo. Therefore, a 50-50 call.

The 19-year-old is shouldering a lot of the responsibility at Fulham right now and was called up as a training player into England’s pre-World Cup camp in June.

Tuchel has never seemed to hold Colwill hugely in favour, but the Chelsea man is playing every week. Centre-back could potentially need an extra body considering both Trevoh Chalobah and John Stones are injured.

Was perhaps only back in the squad last month due to the lack of right-back alternatives and it would not be surprising if he missed out this time.

Has never been called up for England before but that is increasingly a grievance for Everton fans, who love the impact the 28-year-old attacking midfielder has on their team.

He’s playing in the Championship for Middlesborough but the former Spurs striker is banging goals in and has 15 goals in 16 games in all competitions. Is it the worst shout to ponder whether Tuchel might take a punt on the 21-year-old?

Scored a cracking hat-trick in the Champions League against AEK Athens that will have impressed Tuchel, but will he get the recall after missing the World Cup?

Shows so much maturity at centre-back for Chelsea, defying his only 20 years of age.

Has had a massive impact on Tottenham since returning from his ACL injury and might just be in with an outside shout of a return to the England setup.

Was the third-choice goalkeeper last time out but that was largely because Dean Henderson was injured. Will likely have to step aside this time.

Is not enjoying a fruitful season with Nottingham Forest and while he is one of the country’s most talented players, that might not be enough.

Was recalled in March after six years in the international wilderness. An outside bet.

Playing more regularly for Newcastle but is now 34 years of age and perhaps Tuchel will feel his time has come and gone.

Continues to shine at Spurs and it does feel like only a matter of time before the versatile 20-year-old progresses from the England youth setup to the senior team.

This is a rogue shout, but Bogle has been so impressive at wing-back for Leeds that perhaps Tuchel might take a look.

Was only called up with one game left of the last international break due to enough players dropping out that the squad needed cover. Would be surprising if he is back in.

Has played for England on four occasions in the past but Tuchel doesn’t fancy him in his midfield and it would be a shock if the Palace man were included.

By Anthony Nolan | 03 Nov 2026 00:28, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 15:10

Liverpool will travel to take on Turkish giants Fenerbahce on Wednesday, battling to keep their perfect start to the Champions League's league-phase intact.

Andoni Iraola's Reds were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal on Sunday afternoon, though the boss will be pleased with his team's performance overall - as well as the fact there were no new injuries from the intense showdown at Anfield.

With that in mind, Alisson Becker should start in goal this week, shielded by captain Virgil van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet at centre-back, while youngster Giovanni Leoni is closing in on a return to training after more than a year out due to an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Flanking the centre-halves will be Ronald Araujo at right-back and Kostas Tsimikas on the left, with the Greek star likely to come into the XI in place of the rested Milos Kerkez, and both Jeremie Frimpong (hamstring) and Conor Bradley (knee) unavailable.

Ryan Gravenberch was left on the bench against Arsenal, and it has now been revealed that he is suffering from a heel injury, so Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister could pair up in the middle as Trey Nyoni makes way.

In the attacking third, Rio Ngumoha should start on the right wing, with Bradley Barcola on the left, the latter looking for his first goals since netting a hat-trick during the 6-3 win over LASK on matchday two.

Alexander Isak could begin the night on the bench, presenting an opportunity for Lewis Koumas to lead the line, supported by Florian Wirtz from the number 10 role while striker Hugo Ekitike continues his rehabilitation following the Achilles rupture he suffered in April.

#1845. Jack Grealish can't turn down a good night out and his attitude is a problem. IAN HERBERT reveals how the magnetic maverick star sparked concern and now faces a tragedy of missed opportunity

Published: 22:00 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 09:57 EDT, 2 November 2026

At the Pride of Britain awards a week back, we witnessed the brilliant and magnetic side of Jack Grealish, sprinkling stardust as he presented an award to a child of unimaginable courage who counts the Everton player as his hero. 'Footballers are classed as heroes – but these are the real heroes,' Grealish said that night. You could have heard a pin drop.

It was no different when he arrived back at Everton in September, to the delight of the kids awaiting him and his white Lamborghini in the country lane outside the club's Finch Farm training base. 'It feels so good. I think I'm at my best at everything in life when I feel loved,' Grealish said, articulating a very real sense that he was coming home.

He is popular around the club because it can be said without fear of exaggeration that he has a heart of gold.

Only on Thursday, an Everton-supporting father-of-three with a cancer diagnosis that gives him weeks to live disclosed that Grealish had put £10,000 his way. But within hours of that simple act of altruism coming to light, evidence of the other Grealish emerged, as Everton announced he had been excluded from the squad to face Newcastle in the Carabao Cup for failing to turn up for training last week.

It was by no means the first time. Everton sources say there had been similar causes for concern last season. Grealish reported sick ahead of last weekend's game at Arsenal, shortly after the Pride of Britain awards, and has breached Everton's disciplinary code through an unauthorised absence. The stated reason for his absence at Arsenal was illness.

Jack Grealish remains popular at Everton and has a heart of gold, shown by a £10,000 gift to a fan suffering from cancer, but he has since been dropped over a breach of discipline

There were similar causes for concern last season, with his return this summer going against David Moyes' better judgement

Everton's owners, looking for Grealish's glitz and glamour to gloss over their desperately poor and unambitious summer in the transfer window, were keen to bring him back. It was against David Moyes' own better judgement that he accepted his return as part of the deal that brought Iliman Ndiaye's unwelcome departure to Manchester City.

Moyes needed discipline in a thin squad where every player's contribution would count this season. It was an opportunity for the few star players to inspire and shine a light for the younger ones. And therein lies the tragedy of missed opportunity where Grealish is concerned.

He, the quintessential British maverick playmaker in the mould of George Best and Alan Hudson, could be a Goodison hero of these days, yet seems incapable of showing he is bothered, ridding himself of the acolytes and hangers on who are dragging him down, and appreciating what an opportunity football offers him.

Though he likes a drink, it's not so much booze as his attitude, and a struggle to turn down a good night out, which is contributing.

There is no doubt that he still has the skills to be a cherished player. That much was clear in the early stages of last season when he was providing more assists than any other Everton player until a broken foot requiring surgery brought a premature end to his season.

This season he has, as yet, no assists. He has perhaps been frustrated at the number of chances he has created not being converted, though not every winger has Erling Haaland as his support act.

Grealish's patchy attitude to a football life is affecting his game, as he is not taking his man on in the way he used to and does not emit such light on the wing

Look hard enough, though, and you'll see signs that his patchy attitude to a football life is affecting his game. He is not taking his man on in the way he used to and does not emit such light on the wing. Pep Guardiola, at Manchester City, was the first to see this and rapidly made it clear he wanted him gone.

It's not too late for the 31-year-old to become the totemic presence that so many fervently want him to be on Merseyside. Moyes, who sees the wasted potential, has given him abundant support and patience since City left him out in the cold, hoping that he can make him see the opportunity, here.

Thursday night's excellent Carabao Cup win over Newcastle United opens up the potential for an exciting Cup run, with Fleetwood Town awaiting in the quarter-finals. Everton have not won a trophy for 31 years.

The hope must be that the significantly public nature of Grealish's omission – very much a case of Moyes refusing to tolerate another breach – will shock him into action.

It was even the wish of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, present at Thursday night's match, that Grealish would be re-signed to Everton and the PM declared after meeting him at the Pride of Britain awards that the player was an example of the way people 'buy into Everton.'

The collective wish for him to thrive at the club could not be clearer. Only he can make that happen.

#1841. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners 'set sights' on Junior Kroupi swoop - but face competition from two Champions League clubs

By Ben Sully | 03 Nov 2026 01:05, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 02:50

Arsenal have reportedly earmarked Bournemouth star Junior Kroupi as a transfer target ahead of the January window.

The Gunners currently enjoy a three-point lead at the top of the Premier League table after winning eight of their nine matches this season.

Arsenal's league position is largely based on a strong backline that has recorded six clean sheets, the latest of which came in Sunday's hard-fought 1-0 win over Liverpool.

While their backline is their major strength, Arsenal can still improve at the opposite end of the pitch, which is an area Mikel Arteta is keen to address in the winter transfer window.

According to The Mirror, the Arsenal boss has made signing a 'top-class' striker his main priority for the winter market.

Arteta can currently call upon Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres as his main centre-forward options, but the latter has netted just once in 12 appearances this term and has been linked with a potential move away.

The report claims the Gunners have their sights on Bournemouth's Kroupi, although they will need to overcome some major obstacles to pull off the transfer in the new year.

Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain and German giants Bayern Munich are among those obstacles, with the European heavyweights believed to be among Kroupi's suitors.

Even if they can get ahead of their competition, Arsenal would still face the difficult task of convincing Bournemouth to part ways with an important player in the middle of the season.

Kroupi finished the 2025-26 Premier League season as Bournemouth's top scorer after netting 13 goals in 33 appearances.

The Frenchman's progress has been hampered by a foot injury which required surgery and forced him to miss the first two months of the season.

Kroupi has recently returned to the fray with three substitute appearances, although Bournemouth boss Marco Rose is keen to exercise caution with the minutes he gives the 20-year-old as he continues to build up fitness.

With Kroupi being eased back into action, Bournemouth will be reluctant to sanction his departure in January, especially as they will want to keep their key players to give them the best chance of enjoying success this term.

The Cherries harbour ambitions of going a long way in the Europa League, while they are also looking to match or go close to equalling last season's sixth-place finish in the Premier League.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Dejan Kulusevski has been called up by Sweden ahead of the November international break as the Tottenham playmaker continues his recovery from a long-term kneecap injury.
