#1828. Real Madrid: how Franco Mastantuono is faring on loan at Fiorentina

By Axel Clody | 03 Nov 2026 07:08

Franco Mastantuono has finally been getting consecutive opportunities in European football. After a first year of ups and downs at Real Madrid, the young Argentine was loaned to Fiorentina this season and has played in all of the club’s games.

The high point of his spell, which began in August, has been the hat-trick against Venezia in the fourth round of Serie A, a 4-2 comeback win that made him the youngest Argentine player to score three times in Europe’s top five leagues. The first two goals were very much in the right winger’s style: cutting inside onto his left foot and placing the finish.

That result, however, was the only time the Florence side managed to win in Serie A. Fiorentina’s campaign has produced six defeats and two draws, which is why they sit on the edge of the relegation zone.

Mastantuono has not been involved in a goal since, even though he remains the team’s main attacking protagonist. One of the reasons lies in the young player’s biggest challenge so far in Italy, which he admitted himself in an interview shortly after arriving in the country.

Responsible for a third of his team’s league goals, the 19-year-old forward carries the responsibility of being the ‘owner’ of the attacking department in the side managed by Paolo Vanoli. He is always sought out on the wing for an individual move and delivers: he is the leader in ground duels won in the whole of Serie A (48, along with two other players) and third in successful dribbles, 18, alongside Nico Paz.

‘I am always looking to attack, going at opponents and showing personality’ - he explained his profile to the newspaper Gazzetta dello Sport on 4 September.

Thanks to his ability to win individual duels, he also constantly puts himself in a position to shoot, and is third in that statistic in the league too (33, the leader in the Fiorentina squad). He also provides passes for his team-mates’ shots (17 in all, 17th in the league and top in the squad).

The Argentine generates a lot of attacking play, that is undeniable, but the finishing of moves has almost always been negative. He has attempted 33 shots but only nine have been on target. ‘I need to improve in many things, including my efficiency in front of goal,’ he admitted, also to Gazzetta.

Another feature of his game, dribbling, also has issues that hamper Fiorentina and kill the team’s attacks. Mastantuono often wins a one-on-one and, instead of passing the ball, tries another, which makes him lose it.

His success rate in dribbles and ground duels is below half of those attempted (43% and 48% respectively). Among all Serie A players, he is second for possession losses, with 20. Manager Vanoli has already identified the issue, praising the youngster as the only one capable of setting the team’s tempo.

‘He is a talent who needs to be put at the service of the team and must improve his understanding of when to dictate the team’s rhythm. He is the only one who can do that. I told him that, in Italy, we are good at noticing when a player wants to dribble. He needs to improve in one-on-one situations and understand that, if he is double-marked, there will always be a team-mate free. And that means playing as a team’ - he said on 23 October.

This, however, is still common for Franco Mastantuono’s age. It is a natural maturing process. He still looks a very promising youngster, to the same extent as when he emerged at River Plate. He does not see much fairness in the criticism he receives.

‘People demand a lot of me. I understand, I know what they expect of me. Many times they are hard on me, but I try to make the most of it. [...] I do not complain about criticism.

I am a footballer and I understand that. But people talk about things that are outside my control. I just do my job and always try to do it well’ - he told TyC Sports in early October.

Mastantuono is answering some of that criticism on the pitch and, after the frustration of missing the World Cup because of his few minutes at Real Madrid, he was part of Argentina’s latest call-up. The forward, like Nico Paz and other youngsters, will be the future of Argentina in a new era without Lionel Messi and other experienced players.

#1827. Arsenal player ratings vs Slavia Prague: 9/10 statement performance in nervy Champions League win

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal survived a late goal to beat Slavia Prague 2-1 and continue their strong start in the Champions League.

Noni Madueke opened the scoring after charging through on goal in behind and Viktor Gyokeres, who assisted that opener, then got on the scoresheet himself with a wonderful curled finish.

At that stage the Gunners were cruising, but they dropped off significantly in the second half and allowed Slavia to grow in confidence and get back into the game.

Wiktor Nowak scored in the 90th minute as Slavia threatened a grandstand finish but Arsenal did enough to hold on and move up to third in the league-phase standings.

Here is how Matt Verri rated the Arsenal players...

Bit too casual at times with the ball, as he tried to keep himself interested on a very routine night. Did his best to preserve Arsenal’s clean sheet with a truly outrageous save with his fingertips late in the match, but got done with a teasing cross in stoppage-time.

Looked close to his best in attack, flying forward to support Madueke. Perfect cut-back should have been finished by Merino. Bullied Sturm when called into action defensively too. Sloppier after the break as Arsenal’s standards dipped.

Madueke and Gyokeres on target as Arsenal beat Slavia Prague

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

Pressure is on with Saliba back in the squad. Booked for a rash challenge, diving in out wide when he did not need to. But otherwise assured and had one superb burst down the right wing. Key block to deny Ayaosi too.

Rescued Arsenal with two brilliant goal-line clearances in the space of a few seconds. Heroic defending. Stepped up when he needed to and went close to scoring when Madueke crossed to the back post.

Much sharper than he looked against Fleetwood. Dangerous threat down the left wing, but still some moments when he was technically slightly off. However, his runs out wide did seem to bring the best out of Eze.

Even without being at full pelt, Slavia could not live with his running power. Stopped attacks and drove Arsenal up the pitch. Looked exhausted as the second half went on - big surprise he played the full 90 minutes.

Might have gone under the radar but this was a top midfield display. Won eight of his ten duels and played with a nice zip to get Arsenal flowing. Hasn’t had many chances this season but deserves more on this evidence.

Electric. Ruthless finish to open the scoring and he ran the Slavia defence ragged with his direct play. Could easily have had a couple of assists too and improvements off the ball are continuing. Worked really hard.

Wasted two big chances in the first half, surprisingly lacking a clinical edge. But he was confident on the ball and combined nicely with Gyokeres for Arsenal’s second. Just about avoided conceding a penalty after a VAR review.

Confidence was flowing and he gave Vlcek nightmares - the defender just resorted to kicking him. Came close to scoring after some glorious footwork created space. Joy to watch when he glides away from challenges.

Sensational first-half showing. Link-up play was the best it’s been for Arsenal, a massive step up in that regard. Assist for Madueke and had so many nice flicks. Then got his goal with a sublime curled finish. Statement performance.

Rare minutes, particularly with Saliba now back. Too weak in stoppage time when going down and leaving the defence exposed.

Drifted into central areas in a bright cameo. Still a sense he can be too unselfish in the opposition’s box.

Popped up at striker when getting on the end of a goal kick. His lobbed effort bobbled just wide. Not great defending at the near post for Slavia’s goal.

Injected real energy into the team as he tried to get Arsenal going again. Buzzed around the pitch.

#1826. Musah happy with Milan rejuvenation after ‘most beautiful night’: “The fans are incredible”

In the summer, it seemed Yunus Musah was a player on the move, but Ruben Amorim opted to keep him, a decision AC Milan are overjoyed with.

Last summer, it seemed Musah was heading to a permanent exit. Atalanta pursued him all summer and there was interest from across Europe. However, that wasn’t seen as a bad thing by most.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, when La Dea opted against signing him permanently in the summer, most expected the same outcome: a departure. Yet, Amorim opted to keep him and that decision has paid off substantially.

The American has become a core part of the team, and has definitely rejuvenated his career. Indeed, he is beginning to look like the player the Rossoneri hoped he’d become when they signed the youngster from Spain.

Speaking at full-time to Sky Sport 24, the midfielder looked back on his recent rise and admitted that the work was not yet done, as MilanNews relays.

Is it the most beautiful night of the year?

“Yes, it’s definitely been the best night of the year so far. We know that in derbies, when you win, especially at home, the stadium is incredible, the fans are incredible. We learn from every match: we learned from Bologna and we’ll try not to make the same mistakes moving forward.

Today you walked out to a standing ovation: has everything turned upside down?

“I’m happy with the current situation, but football has a short memory and I have to continue like this until the end of the season; otherwise, I know things can change again immediately and here you have to play well every game because there’s always someone who wants your place, you’re at Milan.”

Did you test Rabiot’s goal: was the ball a cross or a shot?

“It was a corner we set up, which we knew Inter wouldn’t pursue. Adrien, no, in my opinion, wanted to put the ball there to create danger, put it there and hope someone would be there. But no, honestly no, I don’t think he meant to shoot.”

#1825. Jose Mourinho identifies key Arsenal star as 'dream' Real Madrid target - and it's not Declan Rice

By Lewis Blain | 03 Nov 2026 07:33

Real Madrid are keeping a close eye on Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori, with Jose Mourinho identifying the Italian as a 'dream' addition to his squad.

The 24-year-old has become an important figure under Mikel Arteta since arriving in a £42m deal from Bologna in 2024, attracting admiration from one of Europe's biggest clubs.

However, the Gunners are in a strong contractual position and have no intention of allowing their defender to leave easily.

Mourinho considers Calafiori his preferred left-back target, with Real Madrid's recruitment staff also sharing their admiration for the Italian international, as per recent reports.

The LaLiga heavyweights have already made initial enquiries about his situation and are weighing up a move next summer, having also been credited with an interest in Martin Zubimendi in recent months.

However, it is the Italy international now on their radar, with his versatility a major attraction, having demonstrated his ability to operate both at left-back and centrally. Madrid believe those qualities could offer Mourinho valuable options across the defence.

Manchester City's Josko Gvardiol is another player admired by the Spanish giants, but Calafiori is understood to be their first-choice option.

Arsenal, however, are determined to retain the defender, whose contract at the Emirates runs until 2029. The Gunners are planning to discuss a new deal with Calafiori in 2027, once they have prioritised extensions for Jurrien Timber, Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice.

Arsenal should have absolutely no interest in entertaining Madrid's advances for Calafiori, who has developed into one of Arteta's most important players.

Initially signed as a centre-back, the Italian has flourished at left-back, with Gabriel and William Saliba's partnership allowing him greater freedom to contribute further forward.

His start to the 2026-27 campaign has been particularly impressive. He scored in the opening minute of the Community Shield against Manchester City, registered assists against Coventry City and Aston Villa, and pipped several alternatives to Arsenal's Player of the Month award for August.

Calafiori offers far more than defensive reliability, combining aggressive forward runs, quality crossing and the ability to drive through opposition pressure.

At 24, he also has plenty of room to develop further, making him an important part of Arsenal's long-term plans.

Mourinho's admiration is understandable, but Arsenal have no reason to weaken their defence by selling a player who has become such an effective part of Arteta's system.

A new contract should be the priority rather than entertaining a potential transfer.

#1824. Heartwarming moment Luis Suarez spots former Liverpool team-mate's son - now Chelsea academy starlet - and poses for a photo

Published: 08:34 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 10:14 EDT, 2 November 2026

Luis Suarez shared a heartwarming moment with former Liverpool team-mate Glen Johnson's son Kobi while at Inter Miami's training complex in Fort Lauderdale.

The 39-year-old Uruguayan was at the ground for the Messi Cup, a youth tournament the MLS side is hosting, and spotted Kobi Johnson lining up with the rest of the Chelsea Under-14s, who are competing in the United States.

The former Liverpool and Barcelona striker went over to the youngster and said: 'I used to play with your dad, I've known you since you were little.'

The one-time Champions League winner then smiled for a photograph with the youngster.

When asked about the chance encounter, teenage Johnson said: 'He (Suarez) just said like, he remembers when I was a little boy and I was quite chubby, and then he asked for a photo.'

Johnson has been at Chelsea from the under-eights and has risen through the ranks, steadily gaining a reputation as an exciting young talent.

Suarez shared a sweet moment with Glen Johnson's son Kobi at Inter Miami's training ground in the US

Kobi Johnson is currently on the books at Chelsea where he is tipped to follow his father into professional football

Suarez and Johnson spent four seasons together at Liverpool between 2011 and 2015

And it is clear to see where he gets it from, with his father Glen having played 357 Premier League games at Chelsea, Liverpool, Portsmouth and Stoke, even winning the league with Chelsea in 2005 and 2006.

It was at Liverpool, however, where the right-back played with Suarez for four seasons between 2011 and 2015 - with the pair were part of a memorable Liverpool team that narrowly missed out on the title back in 2014 after the famous 'Gerrard slip' at Stamford Bridge.

It was during that period too that Suarez was accused of racially abusing former Manchester United left-back Patrice Evra during a Premier League grudge match between the two clubs in 2011.

Suarez was subsequently banned for eight matches after it was ruled that he had used racist language towards Evra.

Johnson controversially publicly defended him at the time, and years later, continued to be conflicted over the incident.

Speaking on talkSPORT in 2019, Johnson said: 'Carra (former team-mate Jamie Carragher) was right to apologise and I'd have to agree with him; I think the timing of it was wrong as the ban was so close.

'But in the club's defence, they were just trying to support one of their players.

'I don't think anyone in that dressing room or at the club believed Luis was racist or capable of being racist.'

While 42-year-old Johnson is enjoying his retirement after leaving the professional game for good in 2018, Suarez is still plying his trade in America at Inter Miami alongside other Barcelona legends like Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi.

#1823. Cardiff 3-3 West Ham: Scott Parker oversees incredible fightback in first game in charge

Scott Parker saw his West Ham side recover from three goals down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff in a thrilling first game in charge.

Jack Moylan’s first hat-trick in English football had Cardiff in cruise control at half-time and Hammers fans venting their anger.

But the Hammers – inspired by captain Jarrod Bowen – fought back in incredible fashion as Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman netted to secure a point.

Parker was confirmed as Hammers boss on Wednesday morning – just 24 hours after Nuno Espirito Santo’s departure – but it was a tough watch for the former England midfielder initially as Moylan had Cardiff 3-0 ahead inside 39 minutes.

Moylan scored a hat-trick on his Republic of Ireland debut against Grenada in May, but this was his first club treble since scoring three for Shelbourne in May 2023.

The draw extends Cardiff’s unbeaten home league run to 10 games over the last two seasons, while West Ham occupy the final play-off place in eighth.

Ex-England footballer Sir Trevor Brooking handed Freedom of the City of London

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

Nuno’s 13-month tenure had ended after the Hammers had won just twice in six matches and lost successive home games to Southampton and West Brom.

Taty Castellanos had hinted at better times ahead, forcing Nathan Trott in to early action after Bowen’s effort had deflected to him.

But the Hammers were behind after Alex Robertson found Moylan in the 11th minute.

Moylan advanced to find the top corner of Mads Hermansen’s net with a ferocious strike from 20 yards.

Hermansen tipped aside Calum Scanlon’s cross and Will Fish headed over as Cardiff probed.

There was no reprieve for West Ham when Perry Ng curled a ball over a static defence after 36 minutes.

Moylan cleverly slowed down for Morato to bundle him over, a clear penalty.

Cardiff had missed their last two spot-kicks, but this time Moylan was entrusted with the responsibility and sent Hermansen the wrong way.

Angry Hammers fans responded with cries of ‘you’re not fit to wear the shirt’, and many of them appeared to be making a swift departure three minutes later.

Joel Bagan’s corner cleared Fish at the near post, but Moylan came in behind him to head home his sixth goal in five games, and his 10th of the season.

Parker sent on Mohamadou Kante and Joel Piroe for Soungoutou Magassa and Castellanos at half-time and there was instantly more conviction from the Hammers.

Bowen floated a delicious pass through after 58 minutes, and Mukasa lifted the ball over Trott and in off a post.

The deficit was reduced further seven minutes later when Piroe flicked on Bowen’s pass and Engels slid home his first Hammers goal.

Kante nearly toe poked the ball past Trott before Kilman touched home Bowen’s brilliant cross, and West Ham almost won it through substitutes Ezra Mayers and Tomas Soucek.

#1822. Aston Villa transfer news: Unai Emery handed huge January transfer boost over £33m midfield target

By Lewis Blain | 03 Nov 2026 07:52

Aston Villa could have an opportunity to strengthen their midfield in January, with Galatasaray reportedly prepared to listen to offers for former target Gabriel Sara.

The Brazilian has attracted interest from several Premier League clubs, including Unai Emery's side, after impressing since leaving Norwich City in 2024.

With the Turkish giants now seemingly willing to negotiate, Villa could have a realistic opportunity to secure a long-standing transfer target.

According to reports in Brazil (via Sport Witness), Newcastle United, Everton and Brighton & Hove Albion are all also interested in signing Sara, alongside Villa, ahead of the January transfer window.

The 27-year-old previously spent two seasons at Carrow Road, establishing himself as one of the Championship's standout midfielders before joining Galatasaray in 2024.

His performances in Turkey have continued to attract attention, with Napoli and AS Roma also reportedly keeping in contact with his representatives.

Galatasaray were reluctant to consider a departure during the summer, when Villa were seeking a replacement for the departed Youri Tielemans, but their stance has now softened ahead of January.

It is believed that the Turkish champions are prepared to negotiate offers starting at €40m (£33m), although reports in Turkey suggest a fee closer to €35m (£30m) could potentially be enough.

While there is no guarantee that Villa or any of the interested clubs will meet Galatasaray's valuation, the willingness to discuss a sale now represents an encouraging development.

Galatasaray's £33m asking price would represent a significant mid-season investment for Villa, although the possibility of negotiating closer to £30m could make the deal slightly more attractive.

Emery needs greater depth in his squad, particularly in central midfield, where additional quality and competition could prove valuable across the second half of the season.

Sara's previous Championship experience means he already understands English football, while his development in Turkey suggests he could return to the Premier League as a more complete midfielder.

At 27, he would also offer a balance of experience and longevity, rather than being purely a long-term investment.

Villa will face stiff competition from the Magpies and the Toffees, but Galatasaray's changing stance gives Emery a genuine opportunity to revisit his past interest.

If the price can be brought down, Sara could represent an attractive January addition for a Villa side looking to maintain its competitiveness across multiple fronts.

#1821. Big game players, big game performances: Player ratings for Milan-Inter from Italian papers

Last night’s win against Inter was proof of the quality within the AC Milan squad, so now it’s a case of continuing on the path upwards.

For Milan, a win in the derby wasn’t essential. Yes, it would always be a big help, but avoiding defeat was the priority, given a 10-point gap would’ve opened to the title leaders. Yet, the Rossoneri were brave and fought for three points, even if most would’ve taken one.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A defining performance of the Ruben Amorim era so far, everyone played their role stupendously – and that includes the Portuguese, who tactically outclassed his counterpart. As a result, the scores from us were rather high in our post-match ratings.

Looking at the ratings from elsewhere, Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) gave the performance an eight, also giving Amorim that score, too.

In terms of the players’ performances, Goncalo Ramos was the lowest, with a still passable score of a 6. However, Ardon Jashari and Davide Bartesaghi were also given these scores, understandable after coming off the bench.

With 6.5s, Koni De Winter, Yunus Musah and Alphadjo Cisse were all very solid, with the latter almost grabbing a fourth in the game. Mario Gila, Strahinja Pavlovic and Sankhoun Diawara were given 7s, as did Luka Modric and the first goalscorer Christian Pulisic.

The Diavolo’s French duo – Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot – were awarded a score of 7.5, whilst Diego Moreira was given an eight for his goal and two assists.

Moving to Corriere dello Sport, Amorim was given an eight again. Ramos scored the lowest again, at a six, whilst Musah, Diawara, Pavlovic and De Winter were given 6.5. Gila, Modric, Pulisic and Rabiot were given 7s. Then, Maignan was given a 7.5, Moreira, again, was given an 8/10.

Finally, Tuttosport’s ratings were largely the same. Ramos was given a downgrade to a 5/10, whilst Moreira was given another eight. The French goalkeeper kept his second-best position with a 7.5 – alongside Rabiot – thanks to his big saves, whilst Diawara was also given a bump up to a 7, thanks to an impressive derby debut.

Elsewhere, Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Musah and Pulisic were given 6.5s, Modric played a 7/10 game and Amorim was given a 7.5.

#1820. RB Leipzig 2-3 Man City: Erling Haaland scores winner to edge Champions League thriller

Erling Haaland struck a late winner as Manchester City edged a thrilling Champions League clash with RB Leipzig 3-2.

City were twice pegged back by the enterprising Germans, who are managed by their former defender Martin Demichelis, but Haaland settled the contest 12 minutes from time.

It was his 14th goal of the season, his 13th in nine career appearances against Leipzig and his 62nd in 61 Champions League games.

City had taken the lead with an own goal from Castello Lukeba but the hosts quickly levelled through Ridle Baku.

Enzo Fernandez restored the lead but City needed Haaland’s late intervention to secure victory after the impressive Antonio Nusa struck a second equaliser.

Despite the win, it was not a night City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma will care to remember.

Leipzig took the game to City early on and Nusa troubled the Italian with a shot from the edge of the box which he fumbled over the crossbar.

Madueke and Gyokeres on target as Arsenal beat Slavia Prague

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Nusa was then involved in a break down the right which led to an opportunity for the inrushing David Raum but his effort was blocked.

Christoph Baumgartner then went close with a curling effort from distance and Brajan Gruda also fired wide from a dangerous position.

City began to settle and Phil Foden curled an effort narrowly wide but they benefited from a huge stroke of luck to take the lead in the 37th minute.

Nico O’Reilly raced on to a long ball from Rayan Cherki but his cutback appeared wasteful. Lukeba, however, did not realise he was under no pressure and ended up bundling the ball into his own net.

Leipzig regrouped at half-time and returned in determined fashion with Nusa and Baumgartner both forcing saves out of Donnarumma.

But the City goalkeeper was badly caught out when he strayed off his line as Baku broke down the left. He may have been anticipating a cross as Baku reached the byline and rifled in a shot at his near post.

Leipzig could have had another moments later as Nusa played in Ezechiel Banzuzi with a backheel but he missed the target.

City rallied and Haaland got his first chance of the game as a Cherki pass was deflected to him but Maarten Vandevoordt kept out the Norwegian’s snap-shot.

They regained the lead after Leipzig allowed Iliman Ndiaye too much space on the left and he whipped in a cross for Fernandez to head home.

Again City could not hold on to the advantage as Nusa drilled a low shot across goal to equalise from a clever pass by Christopher Nkunku.

But Haaland, despite a largely quiet night, was not to be denied and raced in at the back post to slide home Elliot Anderson’s superb low ball into the box.

Both sides hit the woodwork in the closing stages, with Donnarumma almost embarrassed again as Raum’s free-kick looped over him and struck the bar. Cherki also thumped against the bar at the other end.

#1819. Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal: Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres score as Gunners stay unbeaten in Champions League

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Viktor Gyokeres grasped his opportunity as Arsenal beat Slavia Prague 2-1 in the Champions League.

Gyokeres made the most of a rare start, his sixth of the season, with an assist and a stylish goal as the Gunners climbed to third in the Champions League table.

Noni Madueke scored the opener and Arsenal were cruising until the closing stages, when Wiktor Nowak pulled one back to leave Mikel Arteta’s men hanging on in stoppage time.

Gyokeres, whose only previous goal this season was in the Carabao Cup defeat at Fleetwood, was one of six changes Arteta made to the side which beat Liverpool 1-0 at the weekend.

Ben White and Piero Hincapie started in defence in the Czech capital with Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino slotting into midfield and Eberechi Eze a lively presence behind Gyokeres.

There was also a late run-out for youngster Max Dowman, who is suspended domestically but eligible for Europe following his red card at Fleetwood.

Madueke put them ahead in the ninth minute after Gyokeres muscled his marker off the ball on the halfway line and hooked the ball forward into space.

The England winger raced past the defence and slid his angled shot through the legs of Nazar Domchak.

The Slavia goalkeeper then had to come out and block from Gyokeres, tip Merino’s drive over the crossbar and make a fine reflex save from the Spain international.

Arsenal had a mild scare eight minutes before half-time when Tomas Holes got free in the area at a long throw and poked his shot wide.

But the Premier League champions immediately went up the other end and doubled their lead through Gyokeres.

The Sweden striker exchanged passes with Merino as he made his way into the area before opening up his body and clipping the ball across Domchak and in off the far post.

Madueke almost had a second after more good play from Gyokeres, who held up Declan Rice’s pass before laying the ball off to Christos Tzolis.

#1818. RB Leipzig vs. Man City: How to watch Champions League clash, date, time, live stream, TV channel

By Oliver Thomas | 03 Nov 2026 09:00, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 09:03

Gameweek four in the Champions League sees RB Leipzig and Manchester City square off in the League Phase.

The two teams meet for the first time since November 2023 when City secured a 3-2 comeback victory in the UCL group stage, and here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into this fixture.

RB Leipzig vs. Man City will kick off at 20:00 UK time on Wednesday night.

This contest is one of nine taking place on the same evening, with Man City’s English rivals Arsenal and Liverpool among those also in action away against Slavia Prague and Fenerbahce respectively.

This Champions League match will take place at Leipzig’s home the Red Bull Arena, which holds a capacity of 47,800 spectators.

Man City secured a 3-1 victory over the German club in their last visit to their stadium in October 2023 in the Champions League group stage.

RB Leipzig vs. Man City will be shown live on TNT Sports 2 for viewers in the UK.

Fans with the TNT Sports package through their TV provider can watch this game on Sky Go and Virgin TV Go, while this fixture will also be streamed live on Amazon Prime Video in the UK, and on CBS on Paramount+ in the USA.

Match highlights of RB Leipzig vs. Man City will be available on Amazon Prime Video, TNT Sports and via BBC Sport’s dedicated UEFA Champions League Match of the Day show which you can watch live or stream on BBC iPlayer.

You can also view this match on the TNT Sports YouTube channel and both clubs' official YouTube accounts.

Man City are bidding to bounce back from last weekend’s narrow 1-0 Premier League defeat at home to Brighton & Hove Albion, a result which saw them knocked off top spot in the table by champions Arsenal.

Enzo Maresca’s side have accumulated six points from their opening three Champions League matches, most recently thrashing AEK Athens 5-1 at the Etihad with a much-changed side a fortnight ago.

The Citizens, who currently sit 10th in the 36-team League Phase standings, have won four of their previous six meetings with Leipzig and have scored 21 goals in the process, netting at least three goals on four of those occasions.

As for Leipzig, their only triumph over Man City came in December 2021 when they won 2-1 on home soil during the UCL group stage.

Die Roten Bullen, now managed by former City defender Martin Demichelis, are aiming to win their fourth game in all competitions after beating Schalke 04 by a 2-0 scoreline in the Bundesliga last weekend.

However, Leipzig have only won one of their opening three League Phase games in the Champions League this term, most recently losing 4-1 at Real Madrid two weeks ago.

#1817. How Viktor Gyokeres can force Arsenal rethink as it all comes together for striker

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The battle to be Arsenal's starting striker has too often resembled a pillow fight in recent weeks.

Kai Havertz has been well off his best since the international break, while Viktor Gyokeres has struggled to make an impression when given his opportunities.

Both started in that dismal Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood and, regardless of the fact that Gyokeres scored that night, both could have had no complaints if spells on the bench followed.

At last, though, serious punches are starting to be landed. Havertz scored the winner against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday and now, in Prague, Gyokeres responded with one of his best all-round displays - and certainly his best 45 minutes - in an Arsenal shirt.

There had been glimpses of form breaking out. Gyokeres assisted Declan Rice's late equaliser against Bayern Munich last month with a lovely flick.

Here it finally all came together in a superb performance. From the opening minutes against Slavia Prague, Gyokeres was holding the ball up, linking attacks, and playing with the kind of delicate subtlety that has been in short supply in his Arsenal career.

He assisted Noni Madueke's opener with a clever ball in behind and from there his confidence only rose.

When David Raya hammered a pass out, Gyokeres flicked it round the corner on the half volley to Hincapie. There were deft touches to combine with Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino too.

Gyokeres then got himself on the scoresheet with a brilliant passage of play. He laid the ball off to Merino, peeled into space, and when the ball came back to him the finish was sensational. With minimal back-lift, he curled in off the far post.

It was not just Gyokeres' confidence that visibly grew, but the trust his team-mates had in him too. Suddenly Eze was seeking him out with intricate one-twos, backheeling into space.

The striker finished the half with 19 touches, more than he has often managed in full matches.

The context of the match helped. Slavia were poor. Arsenal bullied them, competing with a physicality and playing with a direct intent that their hosts simply could not live with.

Madueke and Eze were both electric and ran their full-backs ragged. There was space on offer and Arsenal ruthlessly exploited it.

Madueke and Gyokeres on target as Arsenal beat Slavia Prague

Slavia Prague vs Arsenal LIVE: Latest score and updates from Champions League

Arsenal player ratings: 9/10 statement performance in nervy Champions League win

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

However, there have been plenty of matches in the past that Arsenal have dominated and yet Gyokeres has still been a passenger, struggling to even register a shot or a meaningful touch. This time, he was central to all that was positive about Arsenal's display.

That is not to say it was perfect. A couple of passes through to Madueke were too rushed, when a more composed decision would have had Arsenal in on goal.

Here it finally all came together in a superb performance

Gyokeres also faded after the break, though that was a reflection on Arsenal's standards dropping rather than the striker doing much wrong. The Gunners were far too casual and gave Slavia encouragement when they were there to be put away.

Arteta will be concerned by that and the casual manner in which Arsenal approached the second half. Their game management was unusually poor and they played like a team that had no regard for what Slavia had to offer.

However, the Arsenal manager will far happier with what Gyokeres produced, particularly in that first half.

There is no question that Arteta's thinking, especially in the biggest games, normally falls towards Havertz. Play like this consistently and Gyokeres can force a rethink.

#1815. Slavia Prague vs Arsenal LIVE: Champions League result, latest updates and fan reaction

Arsenal continued their latest bid for Champions League glory in Prague on Wednesday night. The Gunners travelled to the Czech Republic and left with their unbeaten start to this season's league phase intact, with Mikel Arteta's side ending the night in the top three.

Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres were on target for Arsenal in a 2-1 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League. Madueke broke the deadlock inside the opening 10 minutes, latching onto a flick from Gyokeres before keeping his cool to score his third goal of the season. #1814. It's Golden Bells! England star Jude Bellingham follows David Beckham into underwear modelling in steamy Calvin Klein photoshoot

Published: 11:57 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 11:58 EDT, 2 November 2026

First there was Golden Balls... now there's Golden Bells!

England midfielder Jude Bellingham is starring in an eye-catching underwear campaign for Calvin Klein - almost two decades after David Beckham signed a famous £20m deal to become the face of Emporio Armani.

Real Madrid star Bellingham, one of the stars of England's World Cup campaign, shot the campaign for the fashion giants in the Spanish capital.

The 23-year-old posed in a series of pictures wearing the Icon Cotton Stretch underwear - which retail at around £44 for a pack of three.

'I really enjoyed working on this campaign,' said Bellingham. 'I liked the idea of "the icon underneath" – that confidence starts with feeling comfortable in yourself.'

His underwear campaign follows on from that of fellow Real Madrid and England star Beckham - famously labelled Golden Balls by his wife Victoria.

Beckham signed a three-year deal with Emporio Armani in 2007, shortly after moving to LA Galaxy, with the company revealing sales went up 20 per cent once the news was announced.

Jude Bellingham models the Calvin Klein briefs in a series of images released today

'Calvin Klein is such an iconic brand, so it was great to bring that idea to life in my own way.'

David Beckham models Armani underwear in an advert seen at Macy's in San Francisco

Bellingham celebrated his 50th goal for Real Madrid with a strike against Racing Santander

Bellingham scored his 50th goal for Real on Sunday, in his fourth season at the club since joining from Borussia Dortmund.

The star, who began his career at Birmingham City, netted in a 3-0 win at Racing Santander.

Wearing the No5 shirt in which Zinedine Zidane made his name, Bellingham has now scored one more goal than the great Frenchman for Madrid — in 76 fewer matches.

It comes after he scored seven goals at the World Cup - setting a record for the number scored in one tournament by an England player. It included the final goal in the third-place playoff against France, which England won 6-4.

'Reaching 50 goals with Real Madrid is very special,' said Bellingham. 'Not only for me and my dreams but also for the team.'

'It’s very important for all players to score goals and make a difference in games.'

#1813. Slavia Prague vs. Arsenal: How to watch, date, time, live stream, TV channel for Champions League clash

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 09:19, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 09:19

Remarkably doing battle on the exact same day two years running, Slavia Prague and Arsenal lock horns in the Champions League on November 4, 2026, after previously clashing on November 4, 2025.

The Gunners are setting their sights on replicating or improving on their 3-0 triumph over the Czech champions last season, and both history and recent form suggests that Mikel Arteta's men will make a swift return to winning ways in Europe.

Here, Sports Mole runs through everything you need to know about how to tune into the contest.

Slavia Prague vs. Arsenal will kick off at 8pm UK time on Wednesday evening, or 9pm local time for home supporters.

The contest is one of seven UCL games being played at that time on Wednesday, a list that also includes RB Leipzig vs. Manchester City.

Slavia Prague are welcoming Arsenal to the Fortuna Arena, where the Gunners strode to a 3-0 win last season courtesy of a Bukayo Saka penalty and a Mikel Merino brace.

Jindrich Trpisovsky's side have lost just one of their eight home games this term, although that solitary defeat came in the Champions League - a 3-2 reverse to Lens.

Slavia Prague vs. Arsenal has been selected for coverage on both TNT Sports 1 and TNT Sports 10 for UK audiences.

The latter is only accessible via the red button, but TNT Sports 1 can be found on 408 on EE/BT TV, 521 on Virgin Media and 413 for Sky customers.

Fans with a TNT Sports subscription as part of their TV package can stream the fixture on the corresponding TV app, such as Sky Go and Virgin TV Go.

Alternatively, the game is available to watch on HBO Max, which costs £30.99 per month, or £25.99 a month with a one-year saver plan.

Highlights of Slavia Prague vs. Arsenal will be available to view on the TNT Sports website, as well as their and Arsenal's official YouTube channels.

BBC One will also show Champions League highlights on Match of the Day, which begins at 10.40pm on Wednesday.

Arsenal's unbeaten UCL record is on the line on Wednesday evening, when victory will move the Premier League champions onto 10 points from their opening four games and potentially take them top of the league-phase table if other results go their way.

The Gunners could also extend their unbeaten Champions League run - excluding penalties - to 19 matches, having won 13 and drawn five of their last 18 finishing in normal or extra time.

On the other hand, Slavia Prague have taken just one point from their opening three fixtures and are coincidentally aiming to snap a horrendous 18-match winless run in UEFA tournaments, losing 12 of those fixtures.

The Red and Whites are also searching for their first win against Arsenal at the sixth attempt, having lost three and drawn two of their previous five head-to-heads, and they have never scored a home goal against the Gunners either.

#1812. Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

“He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”

A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more new faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his new-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

“You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

“We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

“I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

“Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

“We can improve quickly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

“We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”

We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

It was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I said before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

It was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

Really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

That’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so quickly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

According to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

"I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS

Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

Kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

Just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford quickly establish possession again.

It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:

To all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys

Another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a big club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

Another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

Igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony shows he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

Jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the new man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

Michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade launched himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

First match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti

Richarlison beats the turf and Ajer punches the air after the Brentford defender wins the foul. Andrews is making another couple of changes: Jensen and Ouattara off, Yarmoliuk and new signing Jadon Anthony on.

Two more Spurs changes too: Maddison and Solanke on, Moore and Richarlison off.

Really sharp save from Kelleher to keep out Moore’s powerful shot from close range. Moore has at least carried a threat for Spurs in the second half, but they are struggling to sustain much pressure.

Tonali with a hit from 25 yards but it deflects comfortably into the arms of Kelleher. Surely a (Kew?) bridge too far for Spurs to dig out any kind of result from here.

De Zerbi looks a little resigned on the touchline, he will know that this is far from his ideal Spurs team on the pitch but that cannot excuse such poor standards.

He fails to open his account for the season. Sent Kinsky the wrong way, but he dragged the penalty just a touch and it cannoned off the post. The lead remains three.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

Spurs are being overpowered here, they cannot cope whenever Brentford come forward. There were appeals for handball against Van Hecke after Janelt swivelled and shot, but the foul is given against Bentancur for bundling over Schade. A complete mess for Spurs.

Any hope that the half-time double change would bring a revival now appear forlorn.

But here is a chance for Mikey Moore! Robertson forward to good effect, and his low cross arrives to Moore at the back post but his shot was too close to Kelleher. Almost crept through his legs.

Well that is surely game over. Cracking strike from Sangare from the edge of the box after a Brentford corner is cleared, they have always been so good at winning those second balls. Driven strike, good save from Kinsky and Kayode is first to the rebound to score from a couple of yards.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Important defensive header from Van Hecke to repel Sangare’s dangerous cross, and we enjoy our first look at a Kayode long throw. Some Strictly Come Dancing moves from Senesi and Collins in the penalty area, and the referee has a word with them. It continues when the throw is taken, and Sensi has a chunk of his shirt, but VAR says the Spurs man was fouled beforehand.

Will we see a different Tottenham in the second half.

Gallagher and Bergvall hooked, replaced by Bentancur and Fernandes who makes his Spurs debut.

15 - There was 15 passes in the build-up to Keane Lewis-Potter's opening goal for Brentford, only Michael Kayode's goal v Wolves in March (19) and Rico Henry's goal v Bournemouth in December (18) have seen more in a Premier League goal for the Bees under Keith Andrews.Busy. pic.twitter.com/8j5RZWFxvH

This has been a dreadful start to the season by Tottenham. Sandro Tonali has barely looked like a £10m player, let alone a £100m midfielder and, maybe unsurprisingly, De Zerbi’s players look like strangers. He will demand a major improvement in the second half. Keith Andrews will be delighted - maybe other than the fact the game isn’t already dead. His team have been dominant.

Brentford utterly dominant, there has been an alarming gulf in industry, precision and class between the two teams. Spurs will surely improve, both in the second half and as the season goes on, but this has fallen well below the standards you expect of a team with European aspirations. If a few of these players never played for De Zerbi again they could have no complaints.

No sign of a Spurs revival at half time, Brentford playing through their press with ease and then have space to run into. Kayode wins his header at the back post but no player was there for the knockdown.

Important block from Ajer after Spurs’s best piece of combination play around the box, before Tonali slashes a volley well over the bar from distance. Cue “what a waste of money” from the home fans.

Richarlison has been non-existent up front for Spurs, bullied by Collins and Ajer.

Tonali with a stray midfield pass to Outtara which rather sums up the Spurs performance so far. Surely there will be sweeping changes from De Zerbi at half time. Solanke, Maddison and Fernandes are the three players you’d have in mind.

“You’re going down with the Fulham,” is the chant from the Brentford fans.

Lewis-Potter swings in a dangerous cross, headed down by Kayode, and Van Hecke stoops to block Outtara’s shot. The whistle goes for a high boot.

This is far from Spurs’s strongest hypothetical team but they are being taken to the cleaners here. Spurs caught in that Brentford man-to-man press again and the ball bounces off Richarlison. Jensen shoots with power from the edge of the box, and Kinsky bats the shot back into danger, and there was Janelt to poke the rebound home. Brentford in total control.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

Spurs’s defence breached again, and Outtara really should have made it two but his first touch was far too heavy and Kinsky was able to clear. Spurs will not be the only team to struggle against this Brentford front three. Schade won the flick on, Thiago swept the ball across the box, but the finish was lacking from Outtara.

Outtara fouls his former Bournemouth team-mate in the Spurs box. A lovely chipped pass forward from Schade releases Thiago in the left channel and another spell of home pressure begins. Lewis-Potter roaming everywhere. Then Brentford win a free-kick which will go in the mixer. Senesi fouled Outtara.

Bergvall floats in a decent cross from the left but it splits Richarlison and Moore. Sweden manager Graham Potter is in the stands watching Bergvall. Van Hecke is known for his progressive passes, but he overhits one through for a Brentford goal kick.

Spurs players not happy with Michael Oliver. Conor Gallagher feels he was pulled back in midfield, before Oliver blows for a 50:50 in Brentford’s favour.

All so simple for Brentford to get at Spurs again, and it takes some excellent defending on the cover from Robertson to deny Outarra who could have been through for a second goal.

Igor Thiago’s header hits the bar but the flag goes up for offside. Brentford’s man-to-man press is smothering Spurs at the moment, they cannot break through it to establish any territory higher up the pitch.

Igor Thiago makes enough of a nuisance of himself to force Senesi to put the ball out for a throw, Brazil vs Argentina in the match up. Brentford just look sharper and more match-ready all over the pitch.

Half a chance for Spurs to reply with a quickfire equaliser, but Tel’s free-kick was tame and deflected through to Kelleher. De Zerbi can have no complaints, it was one-way traffic before the goal.

Well that’s a good early impression from Sangare. He played a lovely one-two before picking out Lewis-Potter for Brentford’s goal.

To say this opening Brentford goal was on the cards would be a mammoth understatement. The home team are finding it so easy to progress the ball to dangerous positions around the Spurs box.

The new man Sangare is involved, playing a one-two at the edge of the area, before picking out Lewis-Potter who was unmarked on the penalty spot. Brentford’s left back popping up in the box, and it is a simple finish.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Pretty much Spurs’s first meaningful foray over the halfway line, but Gallagher’s shot from distance is wild. In other news, Jon Bon Jovi is in the stands. He popped up at a few games at the World Cup.

Brentford continue to make inroads down their left, Lewis-Potter driving at Gray and whipping in a dangerous cross that glanced off Van Hecke at the near post and only just wide of the far post. The corner is swung to the unmarked Sangare at the back post, and his header loops well over.

Brentford continue to look the better team, moving the ball at pace in the final third, but Schade stumbles up against Bergvall in the box. Spurs yet to settle of establish any possession in the game so far.

Collins then catches Gallagher on the foot, as the Spurs man rushed into a challenge to close the defender down. Not much in it.

From that free-kick, Jenson’s delivery was a wicked one: inswinging and flat to the near post, and the ball glanced off Robertson’s head and behind for a corner.

Jensen then tees up Lewis-Potter for an ambitious volley from the edge of the box, and there are hopeful appeals for a handball penalty against Gallagher, and then Collins fails to divert to follow up cross on target.

Not the most distinctive contrast between the two kits, but not as bad as Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season.

Brentford on the front foot in the early exchanges, Sangare involve in their first attack, but Tel runs back to defend well against Kayode.

Schade then wins a free-kick from Van Hecke in a crossing position wide left, the forward’s feet were too quick for the Dutch defender.

The usual rendition of Hey Jude before the game in south west London.

[On three of the back four being new signings] I have a big confidence because all three are very important players with experience and qualities. They have been working for one month and we have no problem with them.

[On Gray wearing the armband] He’s very young but he is a big personality. great behaviour and he deserves to be a captain today. He cannot suffer too much pressure because he is an important player for us for a long time.

[On if there is more business to be done] We have not the right or complete squad today but no excuse we have the qualities to compete against an important team with a clear style, they are very strong in set-pieces and long balls especially.

This will be a first look at new signing Mamadou Sangare for Brentford fans. Lots of people have tipped him to be one of the signings of the summer. I haven’t seen enough of him to give an opinion but it will be interesting to see how he gets on against Tottenham’s first-ever £100m man Sandro Tonali.

There’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

There will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

Archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. New permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

If we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

Brentford XI: Kelleher, Schade, Jensen, Thiago, Ouattara, Sangare, Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter, Janelt, Kayode

Subs: Valdimarsson, Hickey, Henry, Pinnock, Yarmoliuk, Wilson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Your Bees to kick-off the 26/27 season 🐝 pic.twitter.com/nJO5emjgQM

Spurs XI: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Senesi, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Richarlison, Tel

Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett

Our Spurs side on the opening day 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Uh5z221aTc

Starting the season in west London 📌 pic.twitter.com/uglTu9zDvA

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

“He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

#1811. Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta reveals concerns with Champions League win over Slavia Prague

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta admitted he was "very concerned" by Arsenal's second-half performance against Slavia Prague, despite the fact his side picked up all three points.

The Gunners were cruising at half-time of the Champions League clash, leading 2-0 through goals from Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres.

It could have been an even bigger advantage, too, with Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze both having good chances to get on the scoresheet themselves.

However, there was then a significant drop-off after the break. Arsenal were sloppy on the ball and there was an air of complacency to how they approached the second period.

Wiktor Nowak scored for Slavia to set up a nervy finish heading into stoppage-time but Arsenal just about held firm.

"Two very different halves," Arteta said. “The first one, we played a really high level. Exceptional at times I would say. The scoreline should reflect three or fouls goals.

"We didn't do it and at half-time I told them. They are a team with a huge spirit that will keep running, keep believing. They will become even more chaotic.

"We didn't control that at all. Right from the beginning of the first half we were on the back foot. Very sloppy. We gave so many balls away, so many bad clearances, we didn't keep the ball or the structure at all.

"Then you have to suffer because the teams in the Champions League are really good. A lot to learn."

Slavia registered 17 shots in the match, five more than Arsenal, and there was some chaotic moments at the back for the visitors.

#1810. “I can’t change it” – Chivu looks back after three derby defeats to Milan

After last night’s win against Inter, AC Milan have now gone eight games without a defeat in the Derby della Madonnina.

In years gone by, the derby was a result to skip over for Milan. It was a defeat waiting to happen and it seemingly couldn’t be changed and then it flipped. Matteo Gabbia’s goal stopped the streak and in turn, it started a new one.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri entered last night’s game with a run of seven unbeaten and they finished the night with eight unbeaten and a fourth consecutive win. It’s a first in itself for more than 50 years, which is telling.

It’s a result which brought Gerry Cardinale to tears and it’s clear that something has really clicked at San Siro, as the player ratings showed.

Speaking at a press conference after the game, as relayed by MilanNews, the Inter coach spoke about several things, including his unfavourable record in the Derby della Madonnina.

“Compared to last year, there’s something to note about our approach to matches: the superficiality and casualness with which we handle certain situations, where we lack a bit of grit, a bit of determination, a bit of danger perception. But we need to rediscover them.

“We need to be aware that right now, despite a few more points than last year, we’ve lost something that absolutely needs to be rediscovered.”

“I couldn’t, because the forwards have had some problems in the last few days. Bonny only made himself available on the last day after two days with a fever of 39°C and severe nausea and vomiting, so we were forced to find a solution, to make a virtue of necessity, changing the system a bit.

“We knew that, in this type of match, it would be the right thing to have pace on the wings with Spence and Carlos and attack the line a bit more, as well as looking for depth in space with Diouf operating under the striker, looking for both him and Sucic between the lines.

“Unfortunately, sometimes things don’t work out, but, I repeat, we were forced to change.”

“It’s too easy to talk now that Lautaro is injured and the other two forwards aren’t feeling well. These things happen, fortunately not often. We’ll make some assessments, but we’re still happy with our four forwards, in addition to what Lavelli gives us, what Mosconi gives us, and whoever we bring in from the Under 23s.

“But, I repeat, it’s too easy to bring these things up at a time when two forwards aren’t at their best and the third is injured.”

Is there something mental that comes into play in the derby?

“There’s always something mental, I think, and history teaches us this, when you get to play another season after winning.

“So, let’s try not to throw everything away and try to rediscover some determination, some humility in doing certain things, starting with myself, because I’m primarily responsible for everything we do.

“We shouldn’t throw everything away because we’ve reached the tenth matchday and this is the first game we’ve lost. We’ve got 25 points, and last year we’d got fewer, but we’ve always been able to react, we’ve always kept our feet on the ground and our heads down to build a strong season.

“That’s what we’d like to do again this year, because we have this desire and this ambition to have another strong season; we just need to find the way to build it again.”

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta revealed Ezri Konsa had "some issues" that forced him to come off in Arsenal's win over Slavia Prague.

The Gunners won 2-1 to move up to third in the league-phase standings of the Champions League, despite a sloppy second-half display in which they let their hosts back into the match.

Konsa started the match alongside Gabriel, though his place in the side is coming under increasing pressure with William Saliba back in the matchday squad for the first time this season.

Arteta made six changes to his starting lineup in Prague, with Martin Odegaard, Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes among those to drop out of the side.

Asked why he did not substitute Rice and afford him some rest, Arteta replied: "The game required [it] and he did it.

#1808. West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo, "temporary" replacements named ahead of Cardiff City fixture

By Darren Plant | 03 Nov 2026 09:44

West Ham United have announced that they have sacked head coach Nuno Espirito Santo.

When the Hammers were sitting at the top of the Championship table after thrashing Wrexham on September 11, the Portuguese appeared in line to spearhead the club's promotion bid.

However, West Ham have won just two of their last six games in the second tier, one of which came against a Lincoln City outfit who had been quickly reduced to 10 men.

In the two matches since the East Londoners defeated then-leaders Swansea City in South Wales, they suffered home defeats to Southampton and West Bromwich Albion respectively.

Despite West Ham facing Cardiff City on Wednesday night, the club's board have decided to part ways with Nuno.

A statement read: "West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect.

"Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.

"Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed.

"West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future.

"The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway."

Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will oversee the team for the trip to Cardiff.

While Nuno was fortunate to keep his job after relegation from the Premier League, it felt from the outside that he was doing a satisfactory job at the London Stadium.

Had West Ham beat Southampton and West Brom, they would be sitting top of the Championship, emphasising that the 52-year-old has essentially been sacked because of two defeats.

With a favourable fixture list coming up, there was every chance that Nuno would have kept West Ham in contention for the title.

Cardiff, Blackburn Rovers, Preston North End and Portsmouth are their next four games.

Nuno leaves his role with a record of 19 wins, 15 draws and 19 defeats from 53 matches across all competitions.

According to Florian Plettenberg of Sky Sports Germany, Rayan Aït-Nouri is a player to watch ahead of the January transfer window, with the left-back reportedly open to leaving Manchester City. The Algeria international is said to be assessing his options as his representatives explore the market.

Having been linked with Aït-Nouri towards the end of this year’s summer transfer window, Manchester United are interested in signing the 25-year-old and would be prepared to move if a deal became feasible. Personal terms are not believed to be a major obstacle, with the player’s camp understood to be receptive to the possibility of a switch to Old Trafford.
