#1760. Thun vs Hearts - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 03 Nov 2026 15:21

Two teams still searching for their first win in the Europa League league phase will meet on Thursday, as Thun host Hearts at Arena Thun.

The hosts are 32nd in the standings with no points from two games, while the visitors are 29th with one point from two fixtures.

Thun enjoyed a historic 2025-26 season, winning the Swiss Super League title for the first time in their history and in their first year back in the top-flight after earning promotion in 2024-25.

However, Thun have failed to build on that stunning achievement in 2026-27, currently sitting ninth in the Swiss Super League and suffering elimination from both the Champions League and Europa League qualifiers.

Thun, as a result, dropped into the Conference League, where Gian Luca Privitelli's side have lost each of their opening two league phase fixtures, losing 1-0 to Twente and Hajduk Split.

Despite their difficult season to date, Thun did secure a much-needed victory at the weekend, staging a brilliant late comeback to win 5-4 against Lausanne-Sport, ending a five-game winless run.

Thun will also draw confidence from the recent struggles of opponents Hearts, who are also winless in the league phase and head into Thursday's match with just one win in their last six matches across all competitions.

The Jambos most recently endured a disappointing 2-1 defeat to rivals Hibernian in the Scottish League Cup semi-final, with an early goal from Claudio Braga cancelled out by goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath.

In the Conference League, Hearts drew their opening game 1-1 with Nordsjaelland before losing 2-0 to Trabzonspor last time out, leaving them still in search of their first win.

Wouter Vrancken's side have faced a particularly tough time away from Tynecastle Park in recent weeks, winning only one of their last five away matches, although that did come against Motherwell in their last game on the road.

Thun will be without Louis Passavant, Genis Montolio, Fabio Saiz, Mats Seiler and Marc Gutbub due to ongoing injury issues.

Thun are yet to score in the League Phase, and they will be relying on Brighton Labeau and Furkan Dursun to finally open their account on Thursday.

Meanwhile, Hearts are contending with numerous injury problems, including Oisin McEntee, Christian Dale Borchgrevink, Harry Milne, Ageu, Blair Spittal, Tom Renaud and Craig Halkett, while Calvin Miller and Rogers Mato are both doubts.

James Wilson could replace Miller in attack, starting alongside Braga, Josh McPake and Sabah Kerjota, with Laurent Mendy and Tomas Magnusson in the middle of the park.

#1759. Kevin Keegan's iconic Hamburg shirt from 1977 Super Cup against Liverpool sells for £84,500 at auction

Published: 13:58 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 14:10 EDT, 2 November 2026

Kevin Keegan's iconic 1977 European Super Cup shirt has been sold at auction for a jaw-dropping £84,500.

The 1977 European Super Cup was contested between Liverpool, Keegan's former side, and his new club Hamburg. Despite drawing 1-1 in the first leg, Hamburg lost 6-0 in Keegan's first return to Anfield since his signing.

The much-loved legend's No7 shirt formed part of his former Liverpool team-mate Emlyn Hughes' collection. Hughes, who died in 2004, got it in a swap, and it was estimated at around £2,000 to £3,000 by BUDDS auctioneers.

The sky-blue and white adidas shirt features a v-neck style collar and embroidered badge.

The sale comes just months after the football world was plunged into mourning over the death of Keegan, who was regarded as one of the greatest players of his generation.

Keegan began his playing career at Scunthorpe United in 1968, before Bill Shankly signed him for Liverpool. There, he won seven major trophies including three league titles and one European Cup during a six-year spell.

The 1977 European Super Cup was contested between Liverpool, Keegan's former side, and his new club Hamburg

The much-loved legend's No7 shirt formed part of his former Liverpool team-mate Emlyn Hughes' collection

Ever ambitious, Keegan signed for Hamburg in 1977, and it was during his three-year spell in Germany that the 5ft 7in Englishman earned the nickname the 'Mighty Mouse', winning the league title in 1979 and reaching the 1980 European Cup final, where his side were beaten by Nottingham Forest.

It was also at Hamburg that he confirmed his world-class credentials, winning the Ballon d'Or in 1978 and 1979.

The following year he surprisingly joined Southampton before finishing his playing career with Newcastle, where his love affair with the Geordie fans was born during their 1984 promotion-winning campaign.

Keegan made 63 England appearances and captained his country over 30 times, although his only World Cup was an injury-scarred appearance in 1982.

In 1992, Keegan made his first step into management at his former club Newcastle, guiding them into the Premier League and to within touching distance of the 1995-96 title only to miss out to Manchester United.

After leaving St James' Park in January 1997, a brief stint at Fulham followed before he became England manager in 1999, having initially taken on the job following Glenn Hoddle's departure.

Having overseen a disappointing Euro 2000 campaign, Keegan resigned on the back of defeat by Germany at Wembley Stadium, the last match at the national stadium before it was rebuilt.

After his death, an extraordinary sea of flowers surrounded St James' Park to pay tribute to 'The Messiah' who led their charge back into the top-flight in 1984

After England, he managed Manchester City for four years before returning for a brief spell at Newcastle.

Following his death, an extraordinary sea of flowers surrounded St James' Park to pay tribute to 'The Messiah'.

The club wrote a moving statement at the time, which read: 'We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan, one of the most iconic, influential and deeply loved figures in our club's history.

'Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters.'

Milan Futuro battled hard against Pavonese in the rearranged Serie D matchday six fixture on Wednesday night and got a 1-1 draw away from home, despite having gone down to 10 men. It was a result to build on, and build on it they did.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

After a tentative start in which both teams had a few half-chances, it was the home team took the lead in the 20th minute with a shot from outside the box by Cuel that deceived Pittarella.

The Rossoneri equalised in the 22nd minute through Luca Menon, who beat the opposing goalkeeper with a powerful left-footed shot from the edge of the box. After the equaliser, both teams had opportunities to go ahead, but it was level at the break.

The Futuro therefore return to winning ways in the league and climbs to 17 points in the standings, with the second half of the match against Piacenza still to be played after that was suspended due to the referee getting injured.

#1757. Three players who could become Scott Parker's first West Ham signings in January, including £18m striker

By Lewis Blain | 03 Nov 2026 15:40

Scott Parker is expected to take charge of West Ham United after Nuno Espirito Santo was dismissed following a disappointing start to the Championship campaign.

The former Hammers midfielder faces the task of getting his former club back into the promotion picture, with the London Stadium outfit currently eighth and six points behind league leaders Middlesbrough.

West Ham initially looked capable of running away with the title after scoring 16 goals during a four-match winning streak in September, but they have since managed only two league victories in six outings. Consecutive home defeats to Southampton and West Bromwich Albion have ultimately cost Nuno his job.

Parker will inherit a squad that has undergone significant changes since relegation, with around £150m raised through player sales and some of that money reinvested in new arrivals.

However, the Hammers still have weaknesses to address, particularly in attack, and January could provide the new head coach with an opportunity to reshape his squad.

Sports Mole takes a look at three realistic names who could be among Parker's first signings in east London.

A striker should be near the top of Parker's shopping list, with Pablo and Taty Castellanos managing just two league goals between them in West Ham's opening 13 matches. Their combined six goal contributions are hardly convincing, particularly when centre-back Konstantinos Mavropanos has scored five times himself.

Abraham could offer a much-needed alternative, having struggled to secure regular opportunities since returning to Villa Park for around £18m in the summer. The 28-year-old was reportedly close to joining Ipswich Town on loan, but a move to West Ham could appeal given his previous success in the capital, where he scored 30 goals in 82 appearances for Chelsea.

The 11-time England international also has an impressive Championship record, finding the net 48 times in 78 appearances at that level.

With Nicolas Jackson and teenage prospect Brian Madjo seemingly ahead of him at Villa, Parker could offer Abraham the regular football he needs while gaining a proven goalscorer.

Another area requiring attention is the wide positions, particularly with Parker likely to favour his preferred 4-2-3-1 system. Manor Solomon has arrived to provide an attacking threat, but additional competition could help West Ham become more dangerous from the flanks.

Sancho remains without a club after leaving Manchester United in the summer, and the Irons have been linked with the former Borussia Dortmund star for several months. Reports suggest his representatives have contacted several English clubs, including the Hammers, to explore potential opportunities.

His Premier League record of 12 goals and 13 assists in 112 appearances is hardly spectacular, and there would understandably be reservations about taking a gamble on him. However, with no transfer fee required, Sancho could be a relatively low-cost opportunity for Parker to revive a player who has previously demonstrated considerable ability.

West Ham may also need to strengthen at centre-back, particularly with Mavropanos attracting reported interest from Turkish giants Besiktas following an encouraging start to the campaign.

Losing the Greece international would be a significant setback, especially given his importance to the defence, but it could force Parker to revisit an existing target. Rav van den Berg has been linked with the Hammers in recent windows, having cost FC Koln around £11m in 2025.

Parker would have encountered the former Middlesbrough defender during his time managing Burnley in the Championship, potentially giving him a useful understanding of his qualities.

With youngster Airidas Golambeckis already being asked to step into the first team, another centre-back would make sense even if Mavropanos stays.

A January move could therefore address a potential departure while adding a young defender with Championship experience.

#1756. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

Arsenal have reportedly included William Saliba in their travelling squad for Wednesday's Champions League clash against Slavia Prague.

Following almost four months out with the back injury he exacerbated at the World Cup, Saliba returned to full Arsenal training earlier this week.

The 25-year-old was filmed in Tuesday's open practice session, joining in with his teammates at London Colney and appearing in extremely good spirits ahead of his comeback.

Saliba has not played a single minute of competitive football this season, though, so Mikel Arteta is expected to adopt a cautious approach when it comes to his re-integration.

Nevertheless, journalist Simon Collings claims that Saliba will be on the plane to Prague, suggesting that the France international could be in line for his first appearance of the season this week.

Arteta is expected to hold a pre-game press conference this evening after Arsenal land in the Czech Republic, at which point he will no doubt be quizzed for an update on Saliba.

HandofArsenal previously reported that the former Saint-Etienne starlet was in contention to face Slavia Prague, having completed a 'colossal' recovery since the World Cup semi-finals.

Saliba went into the 2026 Mundial carrying the issue, but he was still a regular starter for Les Bleus before having to come off in the 30th minute of their semi-final loss to Spain.

Arsenal and Saliba decided not to go down the surgical route and instead favoured a conservative treatment programme, but there were fears that the centre-back may have missed the remainder of 2027.

However, Saliba's return to individual training last month fuelled the belief that a November return was possible, albeit most likely after the upcoming international break.

Now, the Frenchman could make a quicker-than-expected comeback from the most serious injury of his career so far, one that occurred after he played 50 games for Arsenal in the 2025-26 season.

Barring an exceptional and last-minute Arsenal injury crisis in defence, Saliba will only be on the bench at the Fortuna Arena, as Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhaes continue in front of David Raya.

Konsa has stepped in seamlessly for Saliba during the Frenchman's absence, so much so that Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner recently hailed the Konsa-Gabriel pairing at the best centre-back partnership in the world after Arsenal's 1-0 win at the City Ground.

The ex-Aston Villa man has barely put a foot wrong in red and white thus far, but if Saliba - four-time PFA Team of the Year member and 2026 Ballon d'Or nominee - regains his top level, there is no questioning his spot in the XI.

However, Konsa's tremendous form and the presence of Cristhian Mosquera means that Arsenal can be as careful as they wish with Saliba's re-integration into first-team football.

#1752. Torreense vs Ararat-Armenia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 03 Nov 2026 16:08

Torreense welcome Ararat-Armenia to the Estadio Dr. Magalhaes Pessoa on Thursday evening for round four of the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League campaign.

In their previous European outing, Azul-grenas suffered a thumping 4-1 loss away to Hungarian side Ferencvaros, while the Black and Whites were also convincingly beaten by AZ Alkmaar at the Vazgen Sargsyan Republican Stadium.

Making history as the first side from the Portuguese second tier to ever compete in the competition after beating Sporting CP 2-1 in last season’s Taca de Portugal final, Torreense will be content with how they have started their maiden European campaign.

Having followed up a monumental triumph over Norwegian outfit Lillestrom in their opening fixture by losing back-to-back matches against Sunderland and Ferencvaros, Azul-grenas sit a lowly 28th in the Europa League table, though they are only outside of the knockout phase places on goal difference.

However, Torreense will be extremely disappointed with their start to the latest Liga Portugal 2 campaign as after finishing third and narrowly missing out on promotion to the top tier last season, Joao Nuno’s men have won only two of their opening nine league games to sit 12th in the table with just a two point buffer to the drop zone.

If they are to bounce back from consecutive European defeats on Thursday evening, the key for Azul-grenas could well be to patch up their leaky defence as despite only five teams surrendering fewer goals than them in the league this season, the Portuguese outfit have already conceded seven in their three matches on the continent.

Much like their opposition, Ararat-Armenia are creating history in the Europa League this season as the first Armenian team to ever participate in the main competition, but to the contrast of Torreense, the visitors have not had the start that they would have desired.

Falling to defeat in each of their opening three fixtures, the Black and Whites are one of four sides alongside Marseille, Celtic and Viktoria Plzen that are yet to pick up a single point after three games, though with their inferior goal difference, the Armenian side are currently rooted to the foot of the League Phase table.

On the other hand, Manuel Tulipa will be relatively happy with his side’s progress in the league, as following their first title triumph for six years last season, Ararat-Armenia sit second in the Armenian Premier League table and only two points behind leaders FC Noah, having not lost any of their previous seven outings.

With no prior encounters against Portuguese opposition, the Black and Whites could make history with a victory on Thursday evening, although they will also need to tighten up defensively if they are to climb off the bottom of the table, having shipped 11 goals in Europe so far – two more than any other side in the competition.

French forward Adama Baradji is the host’s only confirmed absentee for Thursday’s clash as the 19-year-old continues to recover from an undisclosed issue that has ruled him out for the last month.

Following back-to-back clean sheets, it is likely that Nuno deploys an identical defence to the one that started against Portimonense on Saturday, with Alejandro Alfaro and Amine Oudrhiri playing just in front of the backline.

Netting the equaliser before the break against Ferencvaros a fortnight ago, it is almost certain that Manuel Pozo is named alongside Dany Jean and Malik Abubakari in the Torreense attack once again this week.

After a fortnight on the sidelines, Ararat-Armenia welcomed midfielder Zidane Banjaqui back to the matchday squad on Sunday, while 34-year-old defender Kamo Hovhannisyan has also returned from injury in the previous week.

Despite playing in the club’s Champions League qualifiers in the summer, Ghanaian forward Paul Ayongo has been left out of the European roster and is the Black and White’s sole miss on Thursday evening.

Having scored five league goals this season, the most of anyone at the club, Arayik Eloyan is likely to be the visitor’s biggest threat in attack this week and will be looking to hit the back of the net for the first time in his career in European competition.

Adriel; David Bruno, Volnei, Stopira, Alcedo; Oudrhiri, Alfaro; Pozo, Jatta, Jean; Abubakari

Joao Bravim; Oliveira, Wilson Valdez, Malis, Grigoryan; Balanta, Carlier; Serobyan, Ambartsumyan, Shaghoyan; Eloyan

Yet to put a point on the board, claiming victory on Thursday’s visit to Portugal looks as though it could be vital for Ararat-Armenia’s chances of potentially progressing to the knockout stages of the Europa League.

However, while they may be struggling domestically, we think Torreense are favourites for victory this week and are backing them to climb out of the elimination places with three points under the lights at the Estadio Dr. Magalhaes Pessoa.

#1751. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1750. 'You have not seen my best’ - Gordon admits he must be ‘more selfish’ after Barcelona

By Alexis Pereira | 03 Nov 2026 16:43

Anthony Gordon has admitted he should be more selfish at Barcelona after a start to life at Camp Nou that has brought three goals and four assists in 14 matches. The England winger spoke to the media ahead of Barcelona’s Champions League clash with Aston Villa on Tuesday (kick-off 8pm UK time), the fourth matchday of the competition, with the La Liga leaders aiming to secure direct qualification for the last 16.

Signed from Newcastle United in May for around £68m (€80m), the 25-year-old has won the trust of boss Hansi Flick on the left of attack, but he has been asked to score more. Barcelona have scored 57 goals in 14 games this season, an average of around four per match, yet Gordon has only three of them. By comparison, Raphinha has 17 and Lamine Yamal 12.

‘I think I can do it more, I can maybe be a little bit more selfish sometimes,’ Gordon said. ‘I think sometimes I maybe pass too much. I should definitely score more goals, but like I said, the reality is goals win games and I am here to win trophies.’

After building his entire career in the Premier League, Gordon arrived in Catalonia with the difficult task of adapting to a new playing philosophy, a different culture and climate, and another language. He surprised Barcelona fans by answering a few questions in Spanish in his first interview and has since been embraced by the squad.

His characteristics fit the collective needs of Barcelona. He has already praised his connection with Pedri, whose vision and technical quality allow him to spot Gordon’s pacy runs in behind the defence down the flank. Without the ball, Gordon also applies a high-intensity press in an attempt to win possession back.

He also said recently that his football intelligence was hugely underrated during his time at Newcastle.

Asked to assess his first 13 games in a Barcelona shirt, Gordon made it clear he has not yet reached his peak but believes he is in a favourable setting to show his talent under the German boss.

‘I would give myself a seven or 7.5,’ he said. ‘I started very well, considering the change of club, country... but I can do more. It will take me a while to adapt completely, and when that happens, you will see my best. You have not seen it yet.’

#1749. AC Milan 3-1 Inter: Five things we learned – individual and tactical success

AC Milan clinched a massive victory in their home derby against Inter on Saturday, with several positives to take from the game as a result.

There wasn’t exactly an excess of optimism before the game among the Milan fans, following what was a poor mid-week defeat and a so-so start to the season. However, we didn’t see much of this in the big game, with two goals scored after just ten minutes.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s almost as if Gerry Cardinale manifested the win before the game and he certainly got to celebrate afterwards, even brought to tears in the mixed zone. He probably learnt a lot from this game and so did we, with several positives to highlight.

Without Diego Moreira, Adrien Rabiot and Mario Gila, Milan and Ruben Amorim struggled a lot in the mid-week clash against Bologna. Fortunately, the trio was back against Inter and the difference was clear as night and day.

All three played a big role, but the true difference-maker was Moreira, who was elctric from the start after bagging an early and lovely assist for Christian Pulisic. Six minutes later, in the 10th minute, he picked up a second from a corner kick, setting up Rabiot.

Inter got back into the game a little with their goal, making it 2-1, and it was a delicate moment in the game when Milan needed to stay focused. And yet again, it was Moreira who brought them out of trouble with a fantastic free-kick just before half-time.

San Siro erupted and the Belgian certainly showed that he has several tricks up his sleeve. On top of the attacking contribution, the Belgian was relentless throughout the game as he helped a tonne defensively until the final whistle.

Milan seem to have a game changer in their hands and it was fitting that he delivered this type of performance in his first Derby Della Madonnina. Especially since Ricky Kaka was in the stands, the player who made Moreira choose the No.22 shirt.

Milan did an outstanding job up front, being as clinical as they could be, but Inter were always going to create chances on the other end. So, it was even more impressive how the Rossoneri managed to contain them, especially in the second half.

There were some struggling moments in the first half, but in that period, Mike Maignan came up big with multiple good saves. One of them was just phenomenal, as he had little to no time to react and it was all about the Frenchman’s reflexes, which didn’t let him down.

That was a crucial moment in the game, with the result being 2-1 for Milan and with an equaliser there, the game could’ve been a lot different.

In the second half, the Rossoneri were a lot more compact and it was more about the players in front of Maignan. Strahinja Pavlovic stepped up a tonne after the half-time mark as he was a tad shaky in the opening 45 minutes, especially against Spence who was bursting down that flank.

Gila was also very solid on the right-hand side and especially when he was on the ball. It’s a completely different team when he’s on the pitch.

Diawara, Musah and Modric also did a very fine job closing down the spaces and handling Inter’s press well, with the Croatian rolling the years back as he was relentless throughout the game.

It was a very impressive defensive performance and especially in the second half of the game, as it seems Amorim’s instructions at the break limited Inter even further.

I purposefully left out Koni De Winter from the previous point because I think the Belgian deserves a section all for himself.

In the absence of Lautaro, Thuram was always going to be the main threat. Not just because he has five goals and four assists in the opening eight games, but also because he has done very well in the derby before.

So naturally, if Milan were to win the game, they had to neutralise the Frenchman and it was clear from the beginning that De Winter’s instructions were to stay close to the striker and not give him breathing space.

De Winter deserves all the praise here because he won almost all of the duels against the striker, effectively frustrating him and getting him out of the game completely. The only memory I have from Thuram was when he dropped almost into his own half towards the end of the game to try and make something happen, but that was not nearly enough.

Aside from his battle with the Frenchman, De Winter also did well with his passing and overall game and was arguably the best Milan defender on the night.

Really positive performance and he needs to keep it up, because conceding silly goals has been a problem for Milan and they clearly have the quality to prevent them.

We already mentioned the brilliant work at the back and the saves Maignan made, but it’s only fair to praise the attack too as they also did a fine job. Milan had three shots on goal until the 90th minute and had scored three goals, which is impressive considering how wasteful the Rossoneri have been in attack in the last few games.

The team started off with the right mindset and put pressure on Inter early on, with some great individual runs such as the one from Moreira. All of the chances were finished with clinical precision, which is exactly what you need to win in the big games.

We already praised Moreira, but Pulisic was also very good as he found the empty space on the opener and buried it to give his side the lead. He then continued playing well between the lines and he was smart about controlling the game after his side was ahead.

Rabiot came in clutch again with yet another goal and a positive performance overall, even if he had to do a bit more running in the second half and focus on the defensive aspect of the game.

I know he failed to score or assist again, but that doesn’t mean Goncalo Ramos was necessarily bad. He pressed quite a bit and he opened up spaces for his teammates. You can clearly see on Milan’s second goal how he pushes Sucic towards the byline so he can’t charge towards Rabiot after Moreira’s corner.

Again, he absolutely needs to be more involved in the box but he’s still a very valuable player on the pitch.

There was obviously a bittersweet feeling coming into the derby after losing to Bologna in such a frustrating manner, but the availability of Moreira, Rabiot and Gila gave Amorim and the fans some enthusiasm prior to the game.

To Amorim’s credit, he picked the correct starting eleven and his team had the right mindset from the start. The coach was aware of Inter’s fragile defending and instructed his team to raise the intensity from the start and apply pressure, which worked a treat with two goals in the opening ten minutes.

Inter then tried to come back into the game and created a few chances, it’s fair to say, but Amorim again tweaked something at the half-time break. His team was more compact and more aggressive after that, which almost completely neutralised Inter.

The coach also waited with his subs, which I think was correct given the team was playing well and there weren’t obvious signs of fatigue. When the changes did come, I think they were spot on.

More importantly, the whole game management was impressive. The game started off with Milan playing in Amorim’s style, which resulted in the goals but also exposed his team and then in the second half, Milan were more compact and not eager to press or attack as much.

On top of that, there were numerous times when the Rossoneri kept the ball, were patient and avoided risk and I think the tempo was dictated by Milan despite Inter having a bit more possession towards the end. Excellent from the coach.

#1747. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1746. AZ Alkmaar vs Juventus - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 03 Nov 2026 16:54, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 16:58

One point apart in the Europa League table, Juventus and AZ Alkmaar are both vying for automatic qualification to this season's last 16.

Set to meet at AFAS Stadion on Thursday evening, Juve have started strongly, but AZ boast a long unbeaten home record in UEFA competition.

More accustomed to dining at Europe's top table, Juventus started their Europa League campaign with a 5-0 cruise at home to NEC, before being made to work much harder for victory over Celta Vigo on matchday two.

Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani both scored as Juve beat Celta and moved top of the table, but they slipped down to seventh with a home draw last time out.

After Zeki Celik had opened the scoring against Rennes, the hosts then found themselves 2-1 down heading into the final half-hour, before Woltemade equalised from the spot.

Since then, it has been quite a mixed bag in Serie A, as the Bianconeri beat Lecce 2-0, then lost to Genoa by the same scoreline, setting up a tense clash with Napoli on Sunday night.

Ahead of kickoff in Turin, Luciano Spalletti's injury-hit side lay 11 points behind the league leaders, below newly promoted Frosinone and just above city rivals Torino.

With his job potentially on the line, Spalletti really had to beat a club he memorably led to the Scudetto in 2023, and stunning strikes from Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga eventually got the job done.

In contrast to their domestic woes, Juventus have lost just one of their last 10 continental games, while scoring at least twice in eight - so they may welcome a return to the Europa League.

Heading into the clubs' first competitive meeting, Juve are seventh in the table on seven points, while AZ sit one point behind in 10th place.

The Dutch side have responded well after an opening-day defeat to Sunderland, first beating Hapoel Be'er Sheva on home turf, then strolling to victory in Yerevan.

AZ simply swept Ararat-Armenia aside at the end of last month, with Brazilian winger Weslley Patati scoring twice in an emphatic 4-0 win.

Now heading back to Alkmaar, they have won 14 and lost none of their last 17 European home matches, dating back to a Conference League clash with Aston Villa three years ago.

However, like Juve, they have recently been below par on the domestic scene: Leeroy Echteld's side have only taken one point from their last four league games, leaving them fifth in the Eredivisie.

Amid a tough run of fixtures, they lost 2-0 at Feyenoord, drew 2-2 with Cambuur and were beaten 2-0 at home by Twente, before losing 1-0 to Ajax in Amsterdam.

Juventus are still missing several men, as their relentless injury crisis continues.

Celik and Nico Gonzalez most recently joined Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Francisco Conceicao, Kamil Grabara and captain Manuel Locatelli on the sidelines.

Furthermore, Weston McKennie, Juan Cabal and Alajbegovic all sustained knocks against Napoli, though they are expected to play some part in Alkmaar.

With Jeff Ekhator just returning, there are few alternatives to Kolo Muani and Woltemade, the latter of whom is joint-top scorer in this season's Europa League with three goals.

AZ forwards Patati and Mexx Meerdink have notched two apiece, and they are likely to feature in the hosts' front three.

Ayoub Oufkir is another option, as he returns from a domestic suspension, while rising star Kees Smit should be back on the bench after recovering from injury.

Club captain Peer Koopmeiners could come up against his big brother Teun, who scored 35 times in 116 AZ appearances and may play for Juve in midfield.

De Busser; Dijkstra, Goes, Hoedt, De Wit; Kwakman, P. Koopmeiners; Patati, Stengs, Daal; Meerdink

Vicario; Kalulu, Gatti, Bremer, Cambiaso; Luiz, Sarr; Kolo Muani, T. Koopmeiners, Alajbegovic; Woltemade

They may have made minimal progress in Serie A since Spalletti arrived one year ago, but Juventus are still a force at Europa League level.

With a little luck, the Bianconeri could even threaten AZ's long unbeaten streak on home turf, but the spoils will most likely be shared.

#1744. GdS: An ‘achievable dream’ – why Cardinale left Italy ‘convinced’ by Scudetto bid

Gerry Cardinale left San Siro after the derby win over Inter with a distinct feeling: this AC Milan team can challenge for the title.

Happy as ever about the derby victory, yet still rueful over the defeat to Bologna – a stumble that must not be repeated – La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that Cardinale departed Italy yesterday, bound for New York, where his family and work await him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His thoughts however remain firmly fixed on AC Milan and the tasks that lie ahead, with the renewal of Adrien Rabiot’s contract as a short-term priority and the Scudetto as a cherished, long-term dream.

He admitted as much following the loss to Raffaele Palladino’s side, and he feels it even more strongly now, having won his first derby since taking direct personal control of the club on May 25th.

On Sunday evening, following the final whistle, Cardinale chose not to speak to the team. He had already said everything he needed to say to his players on Saturday at Milanello, aiming to motivate and spur them on to bounce back from the 4-2 defeat against Bologna.

The team took his words to heart: after the derby, Maignan and his team-mates could see the joy on Cardinale’s face, even though he didn’t utter a single word. Amorim, who granted the squad two days of (training set to resume tomorrow) offered his own praise for the team’s performance.

The head of RedBird Capital stepped away from the dressing room, wanting the moment to remain special for the players and the coaching staff, but also because he was deeply moved—tears nearly welling up in his eyes.

Milan, its fans, and the project itself all needed a night like this, and the American knew it. Now, however, Gerry expects the level of performance shown in the derby to be replicated in the upcoming matches, specifically the two before the break: Thursday against Ferencváros and Sunday in Genoa.

These are fixtures that will require managing the post-derby euphoria to ensure there is no drop in focus. While some of the squad celebrated at a well-known Milanese nightclub on Saturday night, the focus shifts to Europe starting tomorrow.

The position in the table needs to be improved following the slip-ups against Benfica and Bournemouth in the first three games. Beyond that, further progress will be required in Serie A.

The only way to close the seven-point gap on Lazio is to avoid any further stumbles like the one against Bologna. On this point, Cardinale and Amorim are in complete agreement.

In fact, while both were delighted by the triumph over their city rivals, that joy only sharpened their regret over the three points dropped against the Rossoblù. Neither the manager nor the owner could stomach the collapse from a 2-1 lead at halftime to a 4-2 defeat.

The two spoke after the derby and are fully aligned: injuries notwithstanding, a Milan side that aspires to be Milan once again – both in Italy and in Europe – cannot afford such lapses in focus.

Beating Inter is satisfying, and remaining unbeaten against their rivals for eight consecutive matches is a positive, but the ultimate priority remains lifting a trophy. City supremacy is not enough, not for Cardinale, and not for Amorim.

The report alleges that Liverpool and Chelsea have already made contact with the Senegal international's representatives.

Interest in the 21-year-old seemingly stems from his lack of Premier League minutes since signing from West Ham United during the summer transfer window.

Diouf, a £40m signing, has made just one start and four substitute outings, with a further two starts coming in the EFL Cup.

With Diouf having a contract at the Gtech Community Stadium until at least 2031, the assumption is that Brentford will reject any interest in his signature.

Nevertheless, the player moved to the Bees expecting to be first-choice. Instead, Keane Lewis-Potter has excelled in the role since the start of the season.

Brentford have a reputation of being shrewd with their transfer business and they would not have signed Diouf without a long-term plan.

Despite the form of Lewis-Potter, Diouf will be called upon as the season progresses, with Brentford attempting to earn a first-ever appearance in Europe.

If Brentford achieve a top-eight finish in the Premier League, any interested club would have very little chance of tempting the West Londoners into a sale.

#1741. 'We owe it to Michael Carrick': Kobbie Mainoo lays down the gauntlet for his Man United team-mates - and claims they are just ONE win away from transforming their season

Published: 10:37 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EDT, 2 November 2026

Kobbie Mainoo says Manchester United’s stars owe it to head coach Michael Carrick and the fans to turn their season around – and believe it might only take one win.

United go into Tuesday’s Champions League tie against Roma at Old Trafford without a victory in nine games and hovering one place above the Premier League relegation zone.

It has left Carrick fighting for his job and led to fans turning on the players after the last home game against Bournemouth which ended with a 3-0 defeat.

Carrick has done his best to shield the squad from criticism, and Mainoo said: ‘I feel like our way to repay that is to also be behind the manager on the pitch and off it, and fight for us as a team.

‘In these tough times you can't expect the fans 100,000 per cent of the time to be happy and cheering when we're not putting out results, you know. We owe it to them to put the results out there for them to cheer again.

‘Of course, it's been a tough season. We've not had the results we've wanted, but you know we need to look forward now. There are big, big games ahead and I feel like we're one win away from changing that.

Kobbie Mainoo says Manchester United’s stars owe it to Michael Carrick and the fans to turn their season around

‘I've been at this club for a long time and I know there's always going to be ups and downs. It's never going to be plain sailing and smooth to the top. So you expect bumps and the best thing about them is you're able to bounce back from them.’

Mainoo signed a new five-year contract in April after re-establishing himself at his boyhood club under Carrick, having asked to leave under the previous head coach Ruben Amorim.

Despite the club’s fortunes taking a nosedive this season, the 21-year-old is determined to help restore the standards that made United great.

‘I'm very grateful to the boss for putting the trust in me as soon as he came in, putting that belief in me and giving me all the advice that he has,’ added Mainoo, who returned to action at Chelsea on Saturday after missing five games.

‘Knowing he's a player who's been at this club and knows the history of this club and knows what it takes to win, I take those words to heart and I try and apply them every day in training and in games.

‘United's a huge club, so I think a lot of people know the values that this club holds and that have been passed down through the people who've worked and played here. I feel like I take some responsibility in that and in spreading the word of what is Manchester United, coming up through the academy. I plan to send that message for hopefully as long as I can.

‘I've tried to take on more responsibility in the team. I want to impose myself more in games and they've definitely helped to do that, giving me more responsibility with taking the ball. There have been ups and downs, but I have to have belief in myself even in these tough times.

‘I feel like in every period of my career so far, I've tried to take positives from them. Even, you know, times that I'm not playing I've learned things and I'm still applying them to this day.’

#1740. Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Dries Mertens celebrating with his team-mates on the touchline after his decisive goal in the 4-2 victory at Sampdoria is typical of the spirit and togetherness that has seen Napoli storm to the top of the Serie A title. It was in dedication to Chelsea loanee Nathaniel Chabolah who recently lost his mother a a nice touch to show that there is much more to life than football, even though they have put themselves in a wonderful position to end Juventusa dominance and end a 26-year wait for the Scudetto.

Five straight wins have put Maurizio Sarria s team two points clear at the top, with the former Empoli manager breathing a new lease of life throughout a team that have always looked capable of competing for the title, yet ultimately fallen short when the pressure to deliver grew. He has transformed the entire dynamics of how Napoli play, with clinical attacking movement combined with a rock-solid defence within a 4-3-3 system that is getting the very best from the players at his disposal. This seasona s statistics proved that point; Napoli are far and away the highest scorers in Serie A this season, while only Inter Milan and Juventus have a better defensive record. Just one defeat in the twenty league games since the opening day loss at Sassuolo is another illustration of just how good Napoli have been this season, with the crushing 4-0 win at AC Milan in early October a sign of what the Partenopei are truly capable of.

Juventus were always likely to be favourites for the Scudetto on Coral and any other football odds site as their dominance of Italian football threatens to extend into its fifth season, so it is perhaps refreshing from a purista s perspective that Napoli have emerged as real contenders to challenge the Bianconeri. Massimo Allegria s side have stormed up the table in ominous fashion following a surprisingly slow start to the season, with eleven straight victories serving a serious warning to Napoli that they will make them fight all the way for the 2015/2016 Serie A title. It remains to be seen how Sarri and his team handle the pressure of having Juventus breathing down their necks, but the fact they have scored twelve goals in their last three games would indicate that

Some may have been surprised by Gonzalo Higuaina s decision to swap Real Madrid for Naples in the summer of 2013, but the 28-year-old has become one of the most feared strikers in Italy. The Argentine international has formed a wonderful strikeforce at the front of a three-man attack, with Jose Callejon and Lorenzo Insigne adding searing pace and skill on either side of a frontman who has made a career from being a true predator inside the box.

Twenty-one games in as many Serie A games this season puts him amongst the most in-form strikers in world football, with his clinical finish which opened the scoring against Sampdoria proving just how good he has been in front of goal. It is the sort of purple patch that any striker worth their salt would dream to be in; Coral have unsurprisingly backed Higuain as favourite to score in their next game against Sarria s former employers Empoli who have kept just one clean sheet from their last five league fixtures. Napoli will need Higuain to carry his rich vein of form throughout the rest of the season if they are to have any chance of maintaining their wonderful pace and sprint clear of the chasing pack.

Napoli have won many admirers across Europe for the quality of football they have played this season, but it remains to be seen if they have the mentality to pass the acid test and keep the momentum going between now and the end of the season. Recent history would suggest that their chances are not great; the Partenopei, then managed by Walter Mazzarri, put themselves in a wonderful position in 2012/2013, only to finish runners-up behind Juventus as the odd slip at the wrong times proved costly in their pursuit of Juventus. A number of third-placed finishes would also suggest that Napoli have lacked the mentality and guile to end their long wait for a Scudetto, but there is real excitement in Naples that the current crop of players have what it takes to stop the Old Lady from making it five titles in a row.

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

#1738. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

#1736. Liverpool's Ryan Gravenberch suffers fracture as Andoni Iraola explains latest injury blow

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 17:18

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has offered further detail on the heel injury that has ruled Ryan Gravenberch out of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Fenerbahce.

On Tuesday morning, Liverpool released a statement announcing that the Netherlands international would be unavailable for the trip to Istanbul and would remain on Merseyside for treatment.

Gravenberch was an unused substitute during Liverpool's 1-0 Premier League loss to Arsenal on Sunday, which was originally believed to have been a selection decision from Iraola, who started Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni against the Gunners.

However, Gravenberch's demotion from the first XI was down to his new fitness issue, which Iraola confirmed in his pre-game press conference was a fracture of the heel.

The Liverpool boss conceded that Gravenberch has shown no improvement over the last 48 hours, although he did not rule him out of Sunday's Premier League clash with Crystal Palace.

“I don’t know, it’s a day-to-day thing," Iraola said when asked if Gravenberch could make the trip to Selhurst Park. "It’s a fracture of the heel. It’s about the pain.

"He has been with some discomfort. The other day against Arsenal he was warming up and he was not fully confident. He hasn’t improved since then.

“But it’s going to be something that every day we ask him, every day we see how he is. If he can be available for the weekend, lovely, he would be a very good help for us. But I cannot tell you right now."

Gravenberch played the full 90 in both of Liverpool's last two Champions League games against LASK Linz and Fenerbahce, and his absence could open the door for Nyoni to keep his place in the first XI.

The 19-year-old made his full Premier League debut in the loss to Arsenal, completing 59 minutes of the contest, after featuring for over 80 minutes against LASK and Villarreal.

Asked how big an opportunity Wednesday's game could be for Nyoni with Gravenberch out, Iraola added: "He has to continue in the same place he has been since the beginning of pre-season.

"He's playing most of the games, we trust him, he's doing very well. I think we have to encourage him to continue improving, continue learning, but he's in a very good place."

Dominik Szoboszlai is another midfield option for Liverpool after recovering from a hamstring injury, as the Reds aim to make it four wins from four in the 2026-27 Champions League.

Iraola's men are one of just five teams with nine points from their first three games and occupy third place in the Champions League table, only below Aston Villa and Paris Saint-Germain on goal difference.

#1734. Crystal Palace vs Hoffenheim - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 03 Nov 2026 17:30, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 17:57

In need of a morale-boosting victory, out-of-sorts Crystal Palace welcome Hoffenheim to Selhurst Park for their latest League Phase fixture in the Europa League on Thursday night.

The Eagles sit 15th in the 36-team standings, while their German counterparts are eight places further back in 23rd spot after the first three rounds of fixtures.

After nine Premier League games, Crystal Palace find themselves languishing in the relegation zone having posted two wins, one draw and a joint division-high six defeats, leaving head coach Pierre Sage under increased pressure.

The Eagles, who have also conceded the most goals in the league (21), suffered their third straight top-flight loss last weekend as they were beaten 2-0 by Tottenham Hotspur, a result impacted by the 13th-minute dismissal of striker Jean-Philippe Mateta.

“A problem with performance” is what Sage clearly needs to address, and the Frenchman – appointed in June to succeed Conference League winner Oliver Glasner – now has two important home games against Hoffenheim and Liverpool to potentially save his job in South London.

Palace’s form in their maiden Europa League campaign has been mixed thus far; they thrashed Lech Poznan 4-0 at home on matchday one before losing 3-2 against Lyon and drawing 2-2 with Besiktas, away displays marked by sluggish starts and spirited yet flawed comeback attempts.

The Eagles will take some comfort from having won three of their last five home matches in all competitions (L2), while they also head into Thursday’s contest unbeaten in seven European games at Selhurst Park (W5 D2).

Competing in major European competition for just the fifth time in their history this season, Hoffenheim have accumulated only three points from a possible nine available at the start of their Europa League campaign (W1 L2).

Die Kraichgauer lost their opening two matches against OFI Crete (2-0) and Besiktas (3-2), but they achieved what Palace could not against Lyon, as they secured a convincing 3-0 victory over the French side a fortnight ago to open their account in the League Phase.

This statement win was part of a three-game winning streak for Christian Ilzer’s side across all competitions, but they have since been brought back down to earth by a DFB-Pokal second-round exit on penalties to Holstein Kiel and a 2-0 Bundesliga defeat against Werder Bremen, losing to the latter last Saturday.

Although five defeats in eight Bundesliga games has seen Hoffenheim slip down to 12th place in the table, already six points adrift of the top four, Ilzer has insisted that he is “not worried” about his team and has taken plenty of positives from their spirited performances.

Returning to winning ways on Thursday is not a given, though, as Hoffenheim have prevailed in only one of their last six European away games (D2 L3) while they have lost all five of their previous meetings with English opposition (once to Spurs, twice to Liverpool and Manchester City).

Crystal Palace trio Ismaila Sarr (groin), Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) and Chadi Riad (knee) all remain sidelined with injuries, but Jorgen Strand Larsen (ankle) and Quinten Timber (hamstring) may be fit to return to the matchday squad.

Despite his Premier League red card, Mateta is available for selection on Thursday and will likely lead the line for the Eagles, with Yeremy Pino, Dwight McNeil, Eddie Nketiah, Dario Osorio and Evann Guessand all battling for starts in the final third.

Cheick Doucoure and Will Hughes are contenders to start in midfield, while Anan Khalaili and Ben Chilwell could both return as wing-backs at the expense of Oscar Mingueza and Tyrick Mitchell.

As for Hoffenheim, their packed treatment room includes ex-West Ham defender Vladimir Coufal, (thigh), Bambase Conte (adductor), Patrick Wimmer (hamstring), Valentin Gendrey (broken leg), Albain Hajdari (foot), Nathan De Cat (knee) and Max Moerstedt (head).

After missing the defeat at Werder Bremen through suspension, Alexander Prass is available to return and could feature as a central midfielder alongside either Leon Avdullahu or Wouter Burger.

Andrej Kramaric contributed to all three goals in the win against Lyon (one goal, two assists) and the 35-year-old will likely be joined in attack by Adam Daghim, Tim Lemperle and top scorer Adam Hlozek (four goals).

Henderson; Canvot, Disasi, Richards; Khalaili, Wharton, Doucoure, Chilwell; Pino, Nketiah; Mateta

Baumann; Abraha, Kabak, Machida, Rots; Prass, Avdullahu; Kramaric, Daghim; Lemperle, Hlozek

Ten of Hoffenheim’s 13 competitive games this season have produced over 2.5 goals, while each of Crystal Palace’s three Europa League matches this term has seen at least four goals scored, so an entertaining contest could be in store on Thursday.

Both teams are desperate for a victory to boost their knockout qualification hopes, but we can envisage the spoils being shared on this occasion.

#1733. Pioli discusses current Milan team, relationship with Ibrahimovic, Scudetto win and Moreira

Stefano Pioli shared some more insight on his time as AC Milan head coach, including the impact of Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Rafael Leao and others.

Pioli was a guest on Sky Calcio Club after Juventus 2-0 Napoli last night, and he revisited the 2021-22 Scudetto win, discussing some of the characteristics of the players, and also drawing comparisons with some current squad members. MilanVibes relayed his words.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Firstly, the coach was asked about if he saw a bit of Rafael Leao in Diego Moreira, given the Belgian was the hero of the derby on Saturday night with one goal and two assists.

“I saw him against Sassuolo too, and he impressed me. He and Rabiot are really strong. Milan played a great match, Maignan made a great save… but with their starting eleven, they’re a really strong team. When Amorim made a few more substitutions, they struggled more.

“It took them a while to get to this point because they had players arriving, probably with some problems, and it takes time to find their rhythm and fitness.

“The results are showing. Modric also still has some important strength. Gonçalo Ramos is doing a great job for the team and is a very good player.”

The discussion about Milan inevitably brought them back to the team that won the league title in 2022. Pioli explained how the playing system was built around the characteristics of the players available, with particular attention to the defensive line and the ability to sustain aggressive football.

“A coach’s skill lies in adapting to a player’s characteristics. At AC Milan, I had players who got lost defending deep. I like that style of play, but it was the best one for those players.

“Kalulu and Tomori also allowed us to take risks. If you want to stay high up the pitch, you need to have significant intensity; anything in between doesn’t work.”

Pioli commented on Leao again, who reached the peak of his powers under the Italian, but also admitted that after the Scudetto not everything went as he would have hoped.

The Scudetto year was devastating. I’ve seen few players of that level. Then he wasn’t, and we weren’t, good. Because when you win, it’s because something special is created in the team. Paolo [Maldini], Ricky [Massara], and I weren’t good – and neither was he – at maintaining and further raising his level.

“He certainly has important qualities. The coach has to understand the players. Rafa is a good player who needs to be encouraged in a certain way.”

During the segment, the background on Roma’s interest also emerged. The Giallorossi contacted Pioli, but at that point the coach had already received an offer from Al Nassr.

“There were times when everyone called me. Even Roma, but I had just received my contract with Al Nassr and I couldn’t break my word.

“I don’t regret going to Saudi Arabia. I wanted to gain experience abroad after my years with AC Milan. The financial aspect and the opportunity to coach Cristiano Ronaldo also played a role.

“If you don’t coach him, you don’t understand how great he is. He’s a champion, obsessed with preparing to score goals. He’s very respectful.”

Pioli spoke about Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Cristiano Ronaldo, two of the biggest profiles that he has had to manage in his career to date.

“Cristiano and Zlatan have a very similar relationship: ‘You’re clear with me and I respect you, if you’re not clear with me, it’s no good.’ I’ve always based our relationship on clarity and sincerity.

“It’s clear that with Zlatan and Cristiano, if you tell them, ‘Look, you’re not playing tomorrow, or you’ll play 60 minutes tomorrow,’ and then I’ll take you off, and you do it or you don’t, it makes a difference.

“I didn’t tell Zlatan something once, but I didn’t tell him because in the rush, I think during the Covid period, we were playing every three days. At the end of the first half it was 0-0, then in 10 minutes we scored 2-3 goals, I don’t remember now…

“Anyway, I made three substitutions: I remember Zlatan, Calhanoglu, and another. So quick, but I hadn’t told Zlatan in advance… The next day [laughs]. he came to me… The good thing about Zlatan is that as soon as he gets over it, the next day it’s as if nothing had happened.”

When asked if Ibrahimovic frequently sulked, Pioli replied: “No, absolutely not. He’s great. But does he tell you? Yes, yes, and then with a tone…

“I always leave my office door open because I like to greet the players and see them. In fact, I had the office changed because I wanted it to be between the locker room and physiotherapy, which they have to go to every day anyway, so every day I greeted all the players, and they came in to see me.

“Every now and then I stopped them, but I didn’t stop them. That day, I didn’t expect Zlatan to come in. He came in and said, ‘I’ll speak today.’ You know, those chairs that move around, I danced for 2-3 minutes, but then it went away.”

Pioli also recalled his first meeting with the Swede, who arrived at Milanello at the end of January 2020 and undoubtedly played a key role in the resurgence.

“Ibrahimovic arrived at Milanello the first day. I waited for him there, and he arrived when it was dark. It was January, the end of January. I followed him in his training, but he also had a knee problem.

“He did a bit of treadmill work, then he came to my office, spoke to me a bit, and I explained to him how I wanted to use him on the pitch, technically and tactically. He said to me: ‘You’re the coach, I’m the player. You respect me, I’ll respect you.’ And that’s what happened.”

Pioli also spoke about the relationship between results and the team, explaining why it’s often more difficult for a coach to put a defeat behind him than to enjoy a victory.

“We coaches don’t enjoy victories because we immediately think about the next game. Defeat, however, stays with you. But what happened to me at Milan was incredibly emotional. Sackings, on the other hand, are difficult; you feel guilty.

“The one in Florence was even more difficult. I had returned with so much willpower and energy. I had returned with so much confidence, and it was a tough blow.”

Finally, a revelation about the possibility of becoming Italy’s coach. Pioli confirmed that he had been close to taking over the national team, but without going into details.

“I’ve touched on it, but not for very long. In our careers, we are the product of all the choices we make. Some are good, some aren’t.”
